- `createStageProps` (function): Draws the scene's props (see the file comment).
- `StageProps` (interface): Props drawn on the stage (see the file comment).
- `StagePropsOptions` (interface): What `createStageProps` takes.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/bake.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/bake.ts)

- `bakeKey` (function): The key of a bake from `source`: the canonical hash of its texture, seed, parameters and size.
- `BakeSource` (interface): What a texture was baked from: everything filled.
- `bakeTexture` (function): Bakes `ref` on `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `newTexel` (function): A fresh texel.
- `normalsFromHeight` (function): Tangent-space normals of a tiling height field (`width` × `height` floats, row 0 at the bottom): Sobel gradients with wrap-around, z out of the surface, scaled by `depth` (a height step of 1 slopes 45° at 2), as RGBA bytes.
- `TextureBake` (interface): A baked texture: its source, its maps and its hash.
- `TextureRef` (type): A texture by id, or by id with its seed, parameters and size.
- `textureSampler` (function): The filled source of `ref` on `registry`.
- `TextureSampler` (interface): A generator ready to sample: its filled source and the function writing texel (x, y) at any integer point.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/codes.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/codes.ts)

- `TEXTURE_CODES` (const): The codes of the texture bake, with their fixes.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/contactShadow.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/contactShadow.ts)

- `CONTACT_SHADOW_CODES` (const): The codes of the level floor bake, with their fixes.
- `contactShadow` (function): The shadow at `d` texels from a block's foot (0–1), fading to 0 at `radius` texels in `steps` bands.
- `ContactShadowOptions` (interface): How the contact shadow at the foot of a block looks.
- `FloorMossOptions` (interface): How moss creeps in from the foot of the blocks.
- `FloorRuneOptions` (interface): The rune circle laid on each dais; sizes in metres.
- `LevelFloorOptions` (interface): What a level's floor is baked from; every part may be left out.
- `levelFloorTexture` (function): A texture generator for `level`'s whole floor: its base texture with moss at the walls' feet, rune circles on the daises and contact shadows along every block's foot (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.ts)

- `DataTextureOptions` (interface): How the textures are made: the look (the bake's own by default) and a repeat overriding the density.
- `TextureMaps` (interface): A bake's textures, by the material slot each fills.
- `toDataTextures` (function): The textures of `bake` for a material's slots (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/brick.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/brick.ts)

- `BRICK` (const): The brick generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/checker.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/checker.ts)

- `CHECKER` (const): The checker generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/dirt.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/dirt.ts)

- `DIRT` (const): The dirt generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/flagstone.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/flagstone.ts)

- `FLAGSTONE` (const): The flagstone generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/grass.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/grass.ts)

- `GRASS` (const): The grass generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/metal.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/metal.ts)

- `METAL` (const): The metal generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/moss.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/moss.ts)

- `MOSS` (const): The moss generator's spec.
- `mossGrowth` (function): Moss growth over a texture of `size` texels: `grow(texel, x, y, cover)` lays moss over the texel when it grows there at `cover` (0–1, about the share of open stone it covers; joints and cracks take it first), and says whether it did.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/planks.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/planks.ts)

- `PLANKS` (const): The plank generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/plaster.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/plaster.ts)

- `PLASTER` (const): The plaster generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/runes.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/runes.ts)

- `paintRune` (function): Writes `mark` onto `texel` (nothing for 0): the inlay's colour, its glow, a little below the stone, smoother.
- `runeCircle` (function): A rune circle: `mark(i, j)` is the mark of the texel whose centre lies (i + ½, j + ½) texels from the circle's centre (i, j whole numbers; the centre on a texel corner).
- `RuneCircleOptions` (interface): The shape of a rune circle, in texels.
- `RuneMark` (type): What a texel of a rune circle is: nothing, a faint line (ring or spoke), or a bright rune or the centre.
- `RUNES` (const): The rune generator's spec.
- `RuneTones` (interface): The colours of a rune circle and how brightly its lines glow (its runes and centre glow at 1).

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/staves.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/staves.ts)

- `STAVES` (const): The barrel-stave generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/stone.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/stone.ts)

- `STONE` (const): The dressed-stone generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/water.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/water.ts)

- `WATER` (const): The water generator's spec.
- `wave` (function): A smooth wave of period 1 in [−1, 1], 1 at whole numbers: a smoothstepped triangle, close to cos 2πt.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/mips.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/mips.ts)

- `linearToSrgbByte` (function): A linear value as the nearest sRGB byte.
- `mipChain` (function): The full mip chain of an RGBA map, level 0 (`data` itself) first, down to 1 × 1: each level the area-weighted box filter of the float level above, averaged as `encoding` says (see the file comment).
- `mipCount` (function): The number of levels of a `width` × `height` texture's full chain.
- `MipEncoding` (type): What a map holds, which says how its levels are averaged.
- `MipLevel` (interface): One level: RGBA bytes, row 0 at the bottom.
- `SRGB_TO_LINEAR` (const): Each sRGB byte's linear value.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/seams.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/seams.ts)

- `measureSeam` (function): The worst seam of `bake` over its channels and both axes (see the file comment).
- `mipProblems` (function): The problems of a mip chain for a `width` × `height` map, one sentence each: the wrong number of levels, a level of the wrong size or data length, the last level not 1 × 1, a colour or roughness level whose mean drifts from level 0's by more than `tolerance` (in linear units), or a normal more than 3% off unit length.
- `periodMismatch` (function): The share of texels (0–1) the sampler writes differently one period away: at (x + width, y), (x, y + height) and (x − width, y − height).
- `rangeProblems` (function): Every value the sampler writes checked against its range (see `RangeReport`).
- `RangeReport` (interface): What `rangeProblems` counts.
- `SEAM_LIMIT` (const): The largest seam delta a tiling texture may have: 2% of the value range.
- `SeamReport` (interface): The worst seam of a bake: where, by how much, and the numbers behind it.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts)

- `assertSize` (function): Throws `GFX_TEXTURE_SIZE` when `entry` cannot bake at `size` with `params`.
- `defineTexture` (function): Defines a texture generator on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `getTexture` (function): The texture `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); throws `CORE_NO_ENTRY` naming the closest ids.
- `sizeProblem` (function): Why `entry` cannot bake at `size` with `params` (a sentence), or '' when it can.
- `TEXTURE_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `texture` entry.
- `TextureEntry` (type): A `texture` entry: one generator.
- `textureKind` (function): Declares the kind `texture` on `registry`, with the engine's v1 and v2 generators, unless it has it.
- `textureParams` (function): The parameters of `entry` with `given` set: every parameter filled; throws `CORE_BAD_SPEC` naming each problem.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/tile.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/tile.ts)

- `BondCell` (interface): One texel's place in a running bond: its cell's column and row (wrapped) and its position inside the cell.
- `cellHash` (function): A seeded value in [0, 1) for the integer point (x, y), with `salt` telling apart uses of one seed (a stone's tone, its crack).
- `palette` (function): A palette's hex colours as sRGB bytes; throws `GFX_EMPTY_PALETTE` naming `what` when it has none.
- `pickTone` (function): One of `colors`, picked by `value` in [0, 1).
- `runningBond` (function): Where texel (x, y) falls in a running bond of `cell` = [width, height] texels over a texture of `size`: courses (rows) of cells, odd courses shifted half a cell, the whole layout moved by `phase` texels.
- `tileNoise` (function): Value noise in [0, 1] over a texture of `size` texels, repeating exactly every `size`: lattice values from `cellHash`, blended with smoothstep, `cells` lattice cells across on each axis (stretched when they differ), summed over octaves and divided by the total weight.
- `TileNoiseOptions` (interface): How `tileNoise` is made.
- `wrapIndex` (function): `i` folded into [0, n) (n a positive integer): -1 → n − 1.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/tslNoise.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/tslNoise.ts)

- `fractalNode` (function): Fractal value noise in [0, 1] at the vec2 node `p` (`fractalNoise` on the GPU).
- `fractalNoise` (function): Fractal value noise in [0, 1] at (x, y): the weighted mean of `octaves` octaves.
- `latticeHash` (function): The lattice value at integer point (x, y) for `seed`, in [0, 1): the CPU twin of the shader's hash.
- `noiseNode` (function): Value noise in [0, 1] at the vec2 node `p`, one lattice cell per unit (`valueNoise` on the GPU).
- `valueNoise` (function): Value noise in [0, 1] at (x, y), one lattice cell per unit: the CPU twin of `noiseNode`.
- `variationAt` (function): The variation factor at world (x, z) metres: 1 + amount (2 · fractal noise at (x, z) / scale − 1).
- `variationNode` (function): The large-scale variation factor as a float node around 1 (`variationAt` on the GPU), sampled at `position`'s x and z (world space by default, so it runs on across meshes and instances): multiply a colour by it.
- `VariationOptions` (interface): How the large-scale variation is made.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/types.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/types.ts)

- `Texel` (interface): One texel as a generator writes it.
- `TexelFn` (type): Writes texel (x, y).
- `TextureContext` (interface): What `create` is given: the parameters (defaults filled), the seed, and the size the texture bakes at.
- `TextureLook` (type): How a texture is magnified: `pixel` keeps texels crisp (nearest), `smooth` blends them (linear).
- `textureSpec` (function): Returns `spec` unchanged, typed: `create` sees the parameters as the schema `params` declares them.
- `TextureSpec` (interface): A generator: its parameters, the size and look it bakes at, and the function that writes its texels.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/v1.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/v1.ts)

- `V1_TEXTURES` (const): The v1 generators, by id.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/v2.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/v2.ts)

- `V2_TEXTURES` (const): The v2 generators, by id.

### [`engine/gfx/thumbnail.ts`](../engine/gfx/thumbnail.ts)

- `compareThumbnails` (function): Compares two thumbnails cell by cell: a cell differs when one of its channels moved by more than `tolerance` (default 24 of 255).
- `MAP_SYMBOLS` (const): The symbols of the map, for the visible objects in order (largest first).
- `STRAY` (const): The per-pixel value of a pixel no object claims (an ID colour the pass did not assign).
- `THUMB_HEIGHT` (const): The grid's height.
- `THUMB_WIDTH` (const): The grid's size: 48 × 27 cells (16:9).
- `thumbnail` (function): Builds the 48 × 27 thumbnail of a frame of row-major RGBA bytes, with the map when the ID pass is given.
- `Thumbnail` (interface): A text thumbnail.
- `ThumbnailDiff` (interface): How two thumbnails differ.
- `ThumbnailIds` (interface): The ID pass's objects per pixel: 0 empty space, k the k-th name of `names` (1-based), `STRAY` unclaimed.

### [`engine/gfx/warmup.ts`](../engine/gfx/warmup.ts)

- `createWarmup` (function): Makes the warm-up registry of `renderer`, counting builds with `counter`.
- `Warmup` (interface): A renderer's warm-up registry.
- `WARMUP_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `WarmupEntry` (interface): What a pool or batch registers: the objects it may show, each made drawable for the warm-up.
- `WarmupProgress` (interface): Progress, after each step: steps done of the total, and the step just done.
- `WarmupReport` (interface): What one warm-up did.
- `WarmupView` (interface): What a warm-up draws: the scene, its camera, how the frame draws it, and what it draws the scene into.

### [`engine/input/actionMaps.ts`](../engine/input/actionMaps.ts)

- `ActionMap` (type): An action map entry.
- `actionMapKind` (function): Declares the kind `actionMap` on `registry` unless it has it.
- `ActionMapSpec` (interface): How an action map is written.
- `defineActionMap` (function): Registers an action map (on the shared registry by default).
- `getActionMap` (function): The action map `id`.
- `listActionMaps` (function): Every action map, sorted by id.
- `PRESETS` (const): The presets, by id.
- `RESERVED_CODES` (const): Codes no action map binds: the pause buttons, and keys the browser or the system keeps.
- `SYSTEM_ACTIONS` (const): The system layer: action → codes.

### [`engine/input/bindings.ts`](../engine/input/bindings.ts)

- `Bindings` (interface): An action map with the player's changes.
- `BINDINGS_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `BINDINGS_FORMAT` (const): The format tag of a saved bindings file.
- `BindingsFile` (interface): A saved bindings file.
- `BindingsOptions` (interface): How bindings are made.
- `BindingsStorage` (interface): Where bindings are saved: the `localStorage` shape.
- `createBindings` (function): Makes the bindings of the action map `map` (an id or an entry), loading saved changes from `options.storage`.
- `pickLabel` (function): What a prompt shows for an action bound to `codes` on `device`: its first code of that device, labelled (the gamepad's only; the mouse's, then the keyboard's; the keyboard's, then the mouse's), or `—` when none is bound.
- `RebindResult` (type): What `rebind` did: the action's codes now, or why it refused and which action holds the code.

### [`engine/input/codes.ts`](../engine/input/codes.ts)

- `codeLabel` (function): What a prompt shows for `code`: `W`, `Space`, `LMB`, `A` / `Cross`, `L Stick Up`.
- `DeviceKind` (type): The devices input comes from; `virtual` is the inspector's (engine/input/devices/virtual.ts).
- `deviceOf` (function): The device a code belongs to.
- `InputSink` (interface): Where the devices write (engine/input/input.ts keeps it): codes going down and up, analog strengths, use.
- `isCode` (function): Whether `code` is one a binding may name.
- `LabelOptions` (interface): How labels are made: the keyboard layout's characters by code, and the pad family.
- `MOUSE_BUTTONS` (const): Mouse buttons by `MouseEvent.button` (0 left, 1 middle, 2 right, 3 back, 4 forward).
- `PAD_BUTTONS` (const): The W3C standard gamepad buttons by index, named by position.
- `PAD_STICKS` (const): The stick directions, each a code whose strength is how far the stick leans that way (after the deadzone).
- `padStyle` (function): The family of a gamepad, from its `Gamepad.id` (vendor 054c is Sony, 057e Nintendo).
- `PadStyle` (type): A gamepad family, for labels.
- `readKeyboardLayout` (function): The page's keyboard layout (`navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap()`, Chromium), or undefined where it is missing.
- `TOUCH_PREFIX` (const): The prefix of the codes touch buttons write: `touch:jump` is the jump button (`touchCode`).
- `touchCode` (function): The code a touch button for `action` writes; every action binds its own (engine/input/input.ts).
- `WHEEL_CODES` (const): The wheel's codes: a notch is a tap, never held.

### [`engine/input/devices/gamepad.ts`](../engine/input/devices/gamepad.ts)

- `createGamepadDevice` (function): Makes the gamepad device over `source`, writing to `sink`.
- `DEADZONE` (const): The stick deadzone by default (the prototype's).
- `GamepadDevice` (interface): The gamepad device: `poll()` once per sample; the right stick and the family for the camera and prompts.
- `GamepadLike` (interface): The Gamepad API's `Gamepad`, as far as the device reads it (a test stub gives just this).
- `GamepadSource` (type): Where pads come from: `navigator.getGamepads`, or a test's slots.
- `radialDeadzone` (function): A stick reading with a radial deadzone `d`, rescaled so the edge still reaches 1.

### [`engine/input/devices/inspector.ts`](../engine/input/devices/inspector.ts)

- `connectVirtualDevice` (function): Gives `host` (the app's inspector host) the page input's virtual device, so `__engine.input` drives the page.
- `virtualDeviceOf` (function): The virtual device of `host`, made on first use.

### [`engine/input/devices/keyboard.ts`](../engine/input/devices/keyboard.ts)

- `attachKeyboard` (function): Listens for keys on `target` (the window) and writes them to `sink`; returns the detach function.
- `isTyping` (function): Whether a key event's target is somewhere the player types.

### [`engine/input/devices/mouse.ts`](../engine/input/devices/mouse.ts)

- `attachMouse` (function): Listens to the mouse over `targets.element`; `lookSpeed` rad/px, `invertY` for flight-style look.
- `LOOK_SPEED` (const): Mouse look speed by default, radians per pixel (about 0.14° a pixel).
- `MouseDevice` (interface): The mouse device.
- `MouseTargets` (interface): Where the mouse device listens.

### [`engine/input/devices/padScript.ts`](../engine/input/devices/padScript.ts)

- `createScriptedGamepad` (function): Makes a scripted pad in slot `index` (0); call `next()` once per frame, before the input samples.
- `parsePadScript` (function): Parses a pad script; throws `INPUT_BAD_SCRIPT` naming each problem.
- `ScriptedGamepad` (interface): A pad that a script moves frame by frame.

### [`engine/input/devices/touch.ts`](../engine/input/devices/touch.ts)

- `attachTouch` (function): Listens to fingers over the page (see the file comment).
- `BUTTON_SLOP` (const): A release on a button or tap control that moved less than this (CSS px) is a tap, however long it was down.
- `HOLD_FRAMES` (const): … and is seen by at least this many frames, so a slow frame never turns a tap into a hold.
- `HOLD_TIME` (const): A hold lasts at least this long (s) …
- `MOUSE_SLOP` (const): The mouse ends touch mode once it moves more than this (CSS px) from the last pointer.
- `STICK_DEAD` (const): The stick's dead zone, as a fraction of its reach.
- `STICK_FULL` (const): Where the stick reaches full speed, as a fraction of its reach.
- `STICK_RADIUS` (const): The stick's reach in CSS px: full speed at its rim.
- `stickAxis` (function): The stick's `[right, forward]` for a thumb `dx`, `dy` CSS px from the centre (`touch.rs:266-272`).
- `StickView` (interface): Where the stick is drawn, in client CSS px: its centre and its knob.
- `TAP_SLOP` (const): A tap on the game moves less than this (CSS px).
- `TAP_TIME` (const): A tap on the game is shorter than this (s), or seen by a single frame.
- `TOUCH_SETTINGS` (const): The touch settings: view settings, never in the hash.
- `TouchDevice` (interface): The touch device.
- `TouchOptions` (interface): How the device behaves beyond its targets.
- `TouchSetting` (type): The `touch` setting: touch mode as detected (`auto`), or forced `on` or `off`.
- `TouchTargets` (interface): Where the touch device listens.

### [`engine/input/devices/virtual.ts`](../engine/input/devices/virtual.ts)

- `createVirtualDevice` (function): Makes a virtual device, holding nothing.
- `playScript` (function): Plays `script` through `device`, calling `step(intents)` once per sim step; returns how many steps ran.
- `VIRTUAL_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `VirtualDevice` (interface): The virtual device.
- `virtualIntents` (function): One step's intents from a virtual sample: `move` turned by the heading `yaw` (the `cam` axis when it holds one).
- `VirtualSample` (interface): What the device holds for one step: actions held and tapped, and its axes by name.

### [`engine/input/input.ts`](../engine/input/input.ts)

- `CameraInputSample` (interface): What the camera takes each frame: mouse look `[right, up]` rad, the right stick `[right, up]`, wheel notches.
- `CameraLike` (interface): A camera as the input reads it (engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts `Camera`): its heading, and its pitch for first person.
- `createInput` (function): Makes the page's input.
- `Input` (interface): A page's input.
- `InputOptions` (interface): How an input is made; in a page every field has its default.

### [`engine/input/intents.ts`](../engine/input/intents.ts)

- `applyIntents` (function): The next step's intents: `prev`'s held keys with `change` applied (`null` clears a key), then normalized with `prev` as the step before, so `p` is the change's presses plus the new edges of `b`.
- `BUFFER_STEPS` (const): How long a press stays buffered by default, in steps: 9, the prototype's 0.15 s at 60 Hz.
- `buffered` (function): Whether `button` was pressed within the last `steps` steps (its press step counts as 0) and not consumed since.
- `consume` (function): Uses up `button`'s latest press, so `buffered` is false until it is pressed again (a jump done, say).
- `consumeAll` (function): Uses up every pending press, so closing a menu does not also attack with the press that closed it.
- `createInputBuffer` (function): A fresh input buffer: nothing held, pressed or consumed.
- `CustomIntentKey` (type): A namespaced key for game code's own intents: `'game:charge'`.
- `diffIntents` (function): The change-point from `prev` to `next` (both normalized, `prev` the step before): each held key whose value changed, `null` for one that went away, and `p` only for presses the edges of `b` do not explain.
- `fromCamera` (function): Turns a stick or keys into a world-space move, so pushing forward walks away from the camera: `axes` is `[right, forward]` (W is `[0, 1]`, D is `[1, 0]`) and `yaw` the camera heading.
- `held` (function): Whether `button` is held this step.
- `InputBuffer` (interface): What a body remembers of its buttons across steps: plain data for a component field (`type: 'object'`, default `createInputBuffer()`), so it is hashed, captured and restored.
- `INTENT_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `INTENT_KEYS` (const): The built-in keys, in the order a normalized object holds them, each with what it means.
- `IntentChanges` (type): A replay change-point's intent part: the keys that changed, `null` for a key cleared, `p` for unexplained presses.
- `IntentKey` (type): A built-in key.
- `Intents` (type): One step's intents, as the sim reads them (systems get them as their second argument).
- `IntentValue` (type): A custom intent's value: plain data, as a replay file holds it.
- `NO_INTENTS` (const): No intents: what a step gets when nothing is given.
- `normalizeIntents` (function): Checks `raw` and returns the step's intents: frozen, keys in order (built-ins, then custom keys sorted), buttons sorted, `p` widened by the edges of `b` since `previous` (the step before; none at the start).
- `pressed` (function): Whether `button` was pressed this step: it went down (or was tapped) since the step before.
- `released` (function): Whether `button` went up on the buffer's step (a tap shorter than a step included).
- `REPEAT_DELAY` (const): Steps a button is held before it first repeats: 18, the prototype's 0.3 s at 60 Hz.
- `REPEAT_RATE` (const): Steps between repeats after the first: 5, the prototype's 0.08 s at 60 Hz, rounded.
- `repeated` (function): Whether `button` fires on the buffer's step as a held key repeats: on its press, then after `delay` steps held, then every `rate` steps (menu cursors, puzzle pieces).
- `updateInputBuffer` (function): Records one step's intents in `buffer` (changed in place, and returned): call it once per step, with the world's `tick`, before reading `released`, `buffered` or `repeated`.

### [`engine/input/script.ts`](../engine/input/script.ts)

- `names` (const): Reads a comma-separated list of names: `South,North`.
- `numbers` (function): Reads `n` comma-separated finite numbers: `0,-1`.
- `parseScript` (function): Parses `text` with `keys` (key → reader); `match` admits extra keys by pattern (`game:charge`).
- `SCRIPT_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `ScriptLine` (interface): One line of a script: how many frames or steps it lasts, its values by key, and its line number (from 1).
- `ValueReader` (type): Reads one value, or returns a problem as a string.

### [`engine/physics/bodies.ts`](../engine/physics/bodies.ts)

- `addBall` (function): Adds a ball prop; returns its id.
- `addBox` (function): Adds a box prop, sized as BoxGeometry (full width, height, depth); returns its id.
- `addCapsule` (function): Adds a capsule prop, standing up (`height` is its straight middle, as CapsuleGeometry's); returns its id.
- `addCylinder` (function): Adds a cylinder prop, standing up (a barrel); returns its id.
- `addProp` (function): Adds a dynamic body of one `shape` (a hull too: a rock), of `PROP_MATERIAL` unless `spec` says otherwise; its id.
- `addSensor` (function): Adds a body whose one collider is a sensor of `shape`: it blocks nothing and detects bodies.
- `applyTorqueImpulse` (function): Turns a body: an angular impulse (N·m·s) about its centre of mass, waking it.
- `driveBody` (function): Sets a kinematic body's velocities so that it reaches `position` and `rotation` when the world steps `dt`.
- `driveMover` (function): Drives a mover's body toward its pose at `sim.time` (the end of the step being run): `driveMover(physics, m, w)`.
- `knock` (function): Knocks a body away from `from`: a push across the ground and up, a tip toward the push and a twist (`knockProp`).
- `KnockOptions` (interface): How hard `knock` hits: speeds, the same for every mass.
- `Mover` (interface): A mover: a kinematic body's path as a function of time (`MOVER_FIELDS` says what each field means).
- `MOVER` (const): A mover with every field at its default (no body).
- `MOVER_FIELDS` (const): A mover's fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('platform', { description, fields: MOVER_FIELDS })`.
- `moverPose` (function): Where a mover is at `time` (s): back and forth along its offset, turning at its spin (shardfall's `amount`).
- `PROP_MATERIAL` (const): The props' material: a hollow wooden crate's (24 kg at 0.75 m), Coulomb friction, a little bounce, and damping that lets a knocked prop slide and roll to rest.
- `PropSpec` (interface): A prop as `addProp` takes it: a body's pose, velocities and options, and its material.
- `RescueLevel` (interface): A level as the rescue reads it: a compiled level (engine/world/level) or anything with these per-tile grids.
- `rescueLost` (function): Puts every dynamic body that fell more than `depth` below its tile's floor, or left the level across the ground, on the nearest walkable tile: at its centre, its lowest point 5 cm above the floor, still, turned as it was, so it drops onto the floor.
- `sensorHits` (function): The dynamic and kinematic bodies a body's sensors overlapped at the last step, in id order.
- `SensorSpec` (interface): Where a sensor goes and how it moves.
- `Trigger` (interface): A trigger: its sensor body and the bodies inside it.
- `TRIGGER_FIELDS` (const): A trigger's fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('zone', { description, fields: TRIGGER_FIELDS })`.
- `updateTrigger` (function): Brings `trigger.inside` up to date with its sensor and returns the bodies that entered and left, in id order.

### [`engine/physics/capture.ts`](../engine/physics/capture.ts)

- `bodyId` (function): The body id of a Rapier handle: `slot + generation · 2³²`.
- `bodyIds` (function): Every body's id, in id order.
- `CAPTURE_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `capturePhysics` (function): The world as a capture: Rapier's snapshot, a fresh copy, with the build that took it.
- `handleOf` (function): The Rapier handle of a body id.
- `PhysicsCapture` (interface): The physics part of a capture: Rapier's snapshot, with the build and version that took it.
- `physicsState` (function): What the hash covers: per body, in id order, its id, translation, rotation, linear and angular velocity.
- `rapierBuild` (function): The Rapier build and version a capture records, `'simd-compat 0.21.0'`: snapshots restore only into the same.
- `restorePhysics` (function): A new world from a capture (checked first: `PHYSICS_BAD_CAPTURE`); the capture is left as it was.
- `STATE_STRIDE` (const): Numbers a body takes in the hashed state: id, translation (3), rotation (4), linear and angular velocity (3 each).

### [`engine/physics/character.ts`](../engine/physics/character.ts)

- `addCharacter` (function): Adds a character's body (a kinematic capsule, group `actor`), its bottom just outside the skin above `feet`.
- `Character` (type): A character's settings, filled: what `createCharacter` returns and an actor's component holds.
- `CHARACTER_FIELDS` (const): A character's settings: `createCharacter` checks a spec against these and fills the defaults.
- `CHARACTER_SETTINGS` (const): The character's settings (the setting `physics.characterGravity`).
- `CHARACTER_STATE_FIELDS` (const): What a character remembers between ticks: plain data in its actor's component, hashed and captured with the sim.
- `CharacterInput` (interface): What a character wants this tick: from the intents (engine/sim/actors.ts) or from its AI.
- `CharacterState` (type): A character's own state, as `stepCharacter` reads and writes it (`CHARACTER_STATE_FIELDS` documents each field).
- `CharacterStep` (interface): What one tick did.
- `createCharacter` (function): Checks a character's settings and fills the defaults; throws `CORE_BAD_SPEC` naming each problem.
- `createCharacterState` (function): A character's state at rest, every field at its default.
- `feetOf` (function): Where a character's feet are: the bottom of its capsule, less the skin (on flat ground, the ground's height).
- `stepCharacter` (function): One sim tick of a character: `steer` turns its intents into a velocity and a move (engine/physics/feel.ts), the controller makes the move (`moveCharacter`), `settle` fixes the velocity from what happened, walls stop the velocity going into them, it pushes what it walked into (both leave at (push·v + m·u)/(push + m)), probes the ground under it and presses a dynamic floor with push × world gravity.
- `StepOptions` (interface): What `stepCharacter` needs beside the character: the step length, the gravities and the one-way platforms.

### [`engine/physics/crowd.ts`](../engine/physics/crowd.ts)

- `addAgent` (function): Adds a queued agent's body now (`updateCrowd` does it through the queue), its feet at `x`, `y`, `z`, moving at `vx`, `vy`, `vz`; returns its id.
- `AgentState` (type): Where an agent is in its life: see `CROWD_AGENT_FIELDS.state`.
- `CROWD_AGENT` (const): An agent with every field at its default: queued, a walker's capsule at the origin.
- `CROWD_AGENT_FIELDS` (const): A crowd agent's fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('pusher', { description, fields: … })`.
- `CROWD_GROUNDED` (const): The grounded heuristic's thresholds (m/s, m): the prototype's 6 units/s, 2 units and 1 unit/s.
- `CROWD_LIMITS` (const): What `updateCrowd` does at most each step by default: bodies added (shardfall's load ramps), corpses kept.
- `CROWD_MATERIAL` (const): The crowd's material: the prototype's density (1 a cubic unit: a walker weighs about 50 kg), no friction under the min rule (an agent slides on everything), no bounce; a corpse's friction, averaged, so it slides to a stop.
- `CrowdAgent` (interface): A crowd agent: its body, its make and what the last readback saw (`CROWD_AGENT_FIELDS` says what each means).
- `CrowdChanges` (interface): What one `updateCrowd` changed: indices into the list it was given, in order.
- `CrowdOptions` (interface): How `updateCrowd` runs.
- `CrowdStepper` (interface): What the crowd's calls read from the sim: the step length (s).
- `killAgent` (function): Kills an agent: its body joins the group `corpse` (the world and props still stop it; the crowd walks through it) with `CROWD_MATERIAL.corpseFriction`, and a flyer falls.
- `knockback` (function): Adds `velocity` (m/s) to an agent or corpse in the world, the same for every mass, waking it.
- `launch` (function): Throws an agent or corpse up: its upward speed becomes at least `up` (m/s) and its speed across the ground is multiplied by `carry` (1; the prototype's kill launch: 1.3).
- `removeAgent` (function): Removes an agent's body now (`updateCrowd` does it for `leaving` agents and old corpses): it is `gone`.
- `setVelocity` (function): Moves a living agent's velocity toward `want` by at most `acceleration × dt` this step: across the ground (a flyer: up and down too), keeping the vertical speed gravity and the solver gave it.
- `updateCrowd` (function): The crowd's step, after the physics step (the phase `readback`), over every agent in id order: reads each body back (feet, velocity, `grounded`); brakes grounded corpses and removes those `corpseTime` old, then the oldest beyond `corpseCap`; removes `leaving` agents; adds the bodies of up to `spawnLimit` queued agents.
- `VelocityOptions` (interface): How `setVelocity` steers.

### [`engine/physics/feel.ts`](../engine/physics/feel.ts)

- `createFeelMeter` (function): A new meter for ticks of `dt` seconds.
- `FeelMeter` (interface): A meter: the report so far and what it is in the middle of measuring.
- `FeelReport` (interface): What `measureFeel` reports.
- `FeelSample` (interface): One tick of a character, as the meter reads it.
- `settle` (function): The feel of one tick, after the move: landing ends a fall (returns the landing speed when above 2 m/s, else 0), a head bump ends a rise, a dash's last tick leaves at most the run speed, and it faces where it dashes or is told to go.
- `steer` (function): The feel of one tick, before the move: timers count, a dash starts, the velocity across the ground follows the momentum model (acceleration, deceleration when let go, skid against its motion, `airControl` in the air), jumps start (coyote time, buffer, wall jump), letting go cuts a rise (`variableJump`), and gravity acts, integrated exactly.
- `Steering` (interface): What `steer` decided for a tick: the move it asks for, and what it started.
- `updateFeelMeter` (function): Reads one tick into the meter (the file comment gives the rules).

### [`engine/physics/groups.ts`](../engine/physics/groups.ts)

- `COLLISION_GROUPS` (const): The collision groups: each one's membership bit and the groups it touches.
- `GROUP_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `GROUP_NAMES` (const): The group names, in table order.
- `groupBits` (function): Rapier's interaction groups for a collider of `group`: its membership bit and the bits of what it touches.
- `GroupName` (type): A collision group's name.
- `queryBits` (function): Rapier's interaction groups for a query that hits the groups named (all of them when none are).
- `touches` (function): Whether colliders of groups `a` and `b` touch.

### [`engine/physics/move.ts`](../engine/physics/move.ts)

- `CharacterHit` (interface): One obstacle the controller met: the body, the point it touched and that surface's outward normal.
- `CharacterMove` (interface): What `moveCharacter` did: the translation it made, whether it ended grounded, and what it hit.
- `isWalkable` (function): Whether `character` can stand on a surface: no steeper than it climbs.
- `isWall` (function): Whether a surface is a wall to `character`: steeper than it climbs, not a ceiling.
- `moveCharacter` (function): Moves a character's capsule by `desired` as far as it can: across first (sliding along walls, up slopes it climbs, pushing props), then down or up alone.
- `MoveOptions` (interface): How `moveCharacter` moves: whether it stands on the ground (and is not rising), and the one-way platforms.
- `partsOf` (function): The Rapier body of a character, with its capsule (its first collider); throws `PHYSICS_BAD_ARGUMENT`.
- `sink` (function): How far a character goes down `by` (< 0) with its sinking `floor`, from where its last move left the capsule: a controller move that leaves the floor out, so a ledge it overhangs holds it up rather than taking it in.

### [`engine/physics/params.ts`](../engine/physics/params.ts)

- `INTEGRATION_PARAMETERS` (const): Rapier's integration parameters, pinned (Rapier 0.21.0's defaults, written out so an upgrade cannot move them).
- `PHYSICS_SETTINGS` (const): The physics settings, path → field; `defineSettings(PHYSICS_SETTINGS, registry)` declares them on another registry.

### [`engine/physics/queries.ts`](../engine/physics/queries.ts)

- `check` (function): Throws `PHYSICS_BAD_ARGUMENT` unless `ok`.
- `Ground` (interface): The ground under a point: its height, its normal and the body it belongs to.
- `Hit` (interface): What a raycast or shape cast struck.
- `hullPoints` (function): A hull's points, checked (at least 4 finite vectors, not all on one plane), flattened as Rapier takes them.
- `HullShape` (interface): A convex hull, for bodies only: the smallest convex solid holding `points` (m, in the body's frame), at least 4 not all in one plane.
- `overlap` (function): The bodies `shape` at `position` overlaps, by id, in id order, each once.
- `OverlapOptions` (interface): An overlap's options.
- `probe` (function): The ground under `(x, z)`: the first surface a ray straight down from `from` meets, or null where there is none.
- `ProbeOptions` (interface): A probe's options: where the downward ray starts, and the groups that count as ground.
- `quat` (function): A rotation as Rapier's `{ x, y, z, w }`, checked and normalized.
- `QuatLike` (type): A rotation: three.js's `Quaternion`, `{ x, y, z, w }` or `[x, y, z, w]`.
- `QUERY_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `QueryOptions` (interface): What every query takes: the groups it hits, and a body it skips.
- `raycast` (function): The first body a ray from `origin` along `dir` strikes within `maxDistance`, or null.
- `RayOptions` (interface): A raycast's options.
- `Shape` (type): A shape, sized like three.js's geometries (see the file comment).
- `shapeArgs` (function): Half extents and radii of a shape, checked: `[kind, ...numbers]` as Rapier's constructors take them.
- `shapeCast` (function): The first body `shape`, moved from `from` along `dir`, strikes within `maxDistance`, or null.
- `ShapeCastOptions` (interface): A shape cast's options.
- `vec` (function): A vector as Rapier's `{ x, y, z }`, checked.
- `Vec3Like` (type): A vector: three.js's `Vector3`, `{ x, y, z }` or `[x, y, z]`.

### [`engine/physics/world.ts`](../engine/physics/world.ts)

- `attachPhysics` (function): Binds `physics` to a sim world and steps it there: the system `physics`, in the phase of that name.
- `bindPhysics` (function): Binds a physics world to a sim world, so `physicsOf(w)` finds it (the scene does this when it starts).
- `BodyChange` (interface): The changes `setBody` makes; each wakes the body.
- `BodySpec` (interface): A body as `addBody` takes it.
- `BodyState` (interface): A body's state, copied: changing it changes nothing.
- `BodyType` (type): How a body moves: pushed by forces and contacts, never, or by the velocity code gives it.
- `ColliderSpec` (interface): One collider of a body: a shape where the body puts it, and its material.
- `createPhysics` (function): Makes a physics world (Rapier initialized at import): empty, with the pinned integration parameters.
- `Physics` (interface): A physics world: bodies, stepping, queries, and the sim's physics hook (`state`, `capture`, `restore`).
- `physicsOf` (function): The physics world of a sim world: its bodies and queries.
- `PhysicsStepper` (interface): What `step` reads from the sim: the step length and the settings (`physics.gravity`).
- `rapierOf` (function): The Rapier world behind `physics` now (a restore replaces it): for the modules beside this one only.
- `scenePhysics` (function): For a scene that asks for physics: a new physics world, with `physics.gravity` declared on `registry` if it lacks it.
- `WORLD_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.

### [`engine/sim/actors.ts`](../engine/sim/actors.ts)

- `ActorComponent` (interface): The component `actor`: an entity the character controller moves.
- `ActorComponents` (type): The components this module reads: `actor`, `animator`, and `oneWay` for one-way platforms.
- `ActorSpec` (interface): What `spawnActor` takes.
- `AnimatorComponent` (interface): The component `animator`: an actor's character animator as plain data, and what its game code tells its body.
- `defineActorKinds` (function): Declares the components `actor`, `animator` and `oneWay` and the setting `physics.characterGravity` on `registry`.
- `FeelOptions` (interface): How `measureFeel` runs: the sim's rate, and the gravity a character falls under unless its settings name one.
- `measureFeel` (function): Measures a character's feel on the standard course (the file comment says what each number is).
- `removeActor` (function): Removes an actor and its body.
- `spawnActor` (function): Spawns an actor in a scene with a physics world: its body, and an entity with the component `actor`.

### [`engine/sim/capture.ts`](../engine/sim/capture.ts)

- `CAPTURE_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `CAPTURE_FORMAT` (const): The capture format tag; a change to what captures hold changes it.
- `CaptureSource` (interface): What a capture is made from: the world's parts, read between steps.
- `cloneData` (function): A deep copy of plain data: arrays, plain objects (undefined values left out), typed arrays and values with `clone()` (three.js's math classes); anything else throws `CORE_NOT_CANONICAL`.
- `makeCapture` (function): Makes a capture from a world's parts: copies of everything, the code held aside.
- `readCapture` (function): Checks `capture` for the world `target` and returns a copy ready to apply.
- `Restoration` (interface): A checked capture, copied, ready for the world to apply; `systems` and `listeners` only for its own world.
- `RestoreTarget` (interface): The world a capture is read for: itself, its component kinds, physics, step rate, setting paths and schedule.
- `ScheduleData` (interface): The world's code as data: systems as `phase:name` in run order, listeners as `type` or `type (once)`.
- `scheduleOf` (function): The schedule of `systems` and a listener snapshot, as data.
- `WorldCapture` (interface): The whole sim at a step boundary, as plain data (code held aside; see the file comment).

### [`engine/sim/crowdBodies.ts`](../engine/sim/crowdBodies.ts)

- `CROWD_BODY` (const): The component `crowdBody`: an entity the stage draws through a crowd.
- `CROWD_BODY_FIELDS` (const): A crowd body's fields, for the component `crowdBody`: its rig and look, where it stands, its rig's state.
- `CrowdBody` (interface): A crowd body: what `CROWD_BODY_FIELDS` holds.
- `CrowdBodyInput` (interface): What a crowd body's rig is told each step (see the file comment).
- `CrowdRig` (type): The rigs a crowd body can have.
- `stepCrowdBody` (function): The rig's sim step for the crowd body `body` of entity `id` (see the file comment): loads it from `body.state` (filling an empty one with the rig at rest), steps it with `input`, saves it back and moves the body to `input.at`.

### [`engine/sim/entities.ts`](../engine/sim/entities.ts)

- `capturable` (function): The entities copied for a capture: plain data only (`SIM_NOT_DATA`) and no object in two places (`SIM_SHARED_DATA`): a capture copies each place separately, so a shared object would come back as two.
- `componentNames` (function): The component names of an entity, in name order, after checking each is a declared kind (`SIM_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT`) holding a plain object (`SIM_NOT_DATA`).
- `eachField` (function): Calls `visit(key, value)` for each field of the entity's component `name`, in declared order, after checking it holds exactly the declared `fields`, each defined (`SIM_UNDECLARED_FIELD`, `SIM_BAD_COMPONENT`); a `live` component must also hold them in declared order, while a stored one is read in that order whatever its key order.
- `ENTITY_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `LiveEntity` (type): A live entity: its id fixed, its components writable.
- `makeEntity` (function): A live entity with `id` (read-only) and the components of `data` (all but its id), in `data`'s order.
- `notData` (function): Checks that `value` is plain data (null, booleans, numbers, strings, arrays and plain objects all the way down) and says where it is not; the path is built only for a refusal.
- `NotData` (interface): Where a value stops being plain data, and what is there; undefined when it is all plain data.
- `placeComponent` (function): Puts `component` on a live `entity` as `name`, keeping components in name order (later ones are put back after).

### [`engine/sim/levelBodies.ts`](../engine/sim/levelBodies.ts)

- `addLevelBodies` (function): Adds a level's bodies (one fixed body: the ground slab and its colliders) and returns the body's id.
- `LEVEL_FRICTION` (const): The level's friction: the prototype's hall.

### [`engine/sim/props.ts`](../engine/sim/props.ts)

- `definePropKinds` (function): Declares the component `sceneProp` on `registry` (once).
- `hitProp` (function): Hits the prop `id` from `from` (m): calls its `hit` hook, whose `knock(more)` knocks its body away from `from` with `strength` under `more` (engine/physics/bodies.ts's `knock`: 4.6875 m/s across, 2.5 m/s up, no twist by default).
- `removeProp` (function): Removes a prop: its entity and its body.
- `SCENE_PROP_FIELDS` (const): The component `sceneProp`'s fields.
- `ScenePropComponent` (interface): The component `sceneProp`: a prop standing in a scene.
- `ScenePropComponents` (type): The components this module reads.
- `spawnProp` (function): Stands the prop of `placement` in the scene: its body (when it has one; the scene needs physics then) and an entity with the component `sceneProp`.

### [`engine/sim/queryView.ts`](../engine/sim/queryView.ts)

- `queryView` (function): The read-only view of a physics world.
- `QueryView` (type): The physics queries, read-only: what presentation code may ask of the sim's physics.
- `queryViewOf` (function): The read-only view of a sim world's physics.

### [`engine/sim/replay.ts`](../engine/sim/replay.ts)

- `CHECKPOINT_STEPS` (const): Steps between checkpoint hashes when a replay names none (§6.5 item 6).
- `checkpointsOf` (function): The steps a replay hashes: 0 and the last, plus those its goldens name (every platform's), else every 60.
- `checkReplay` (function): Checks a replay's whole shape and returns it typed; throws `SIM_BAD_REPLAY` listing the first problems.
- `firstDifference` (function): The first step at which two runs' hashes differ, over the steps both took; undefined when they agree.
- `InputChange` (type): One change-point's content: intent keys, setting values and a dev action.
- `InputEntry` (type): A change-point: after `step` steps, before the next.
- `judgeRuns` (function): Judges runs (their hashes) of `replay` on `platform` (see `Verdict`).
- `Parting` (interface): Where two runs part at one step: the parts and entities whose trace digests differ, and the first fields.
- `partingOf` (function): Compares two runs' views of the same step: `trace()` digests by part and entity, then `diffStates`.
- `PLATFORM_KEYS` (const): Every golden key a platform may have: `linux-x64`, `darwin-arm64`, …
- `Playback` (interface): A played replay: its session (at the step it stopped) and the hashes it took, by step.
- `PlayOptions` (interface): How a replay plays: where its scene is, which steps to hash, and where to stop.
- `playReplay` (function): Plays a replay (checked first) from step 0 and hashes its checkpoints.
- `Replay` (interface): A replay, as its file holds it (PLAN.md §8.4).
- `REPLAY_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `REPLAY_FORMAT` (const): The replay format tag; a change to what replays hold changes it.
- `REPLAY_KEYS` (const): The keys a replay has, in file order.
- `StepView` (interface): One run's view of a step, as `x replay --bisect` compares two.
- `Verdict` (type): The verdict on runs of a replay (§6.5 item 8): against this platform's goldens when it has them (`mismatch` names the first run and step that miss), else, when another platform recorded it, the runs against each other (`other platform`, or `unstable` naming the first run that parts from run 0), else `none`.

### [`engine/sim/scene.ts`](../engine/sim/scene.ts)

- `checkSeed` (function): Returns `seed` (1 when absent; -0 as 0); throws `SIM_BAD_SEED` naming `where` unless it is a whole number from 0.
- `createSession` (function): Starts a scene as a recorded session: `startScene`, plus the recording.
- `defineScene` (function): Registers a scene on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `getScene` (function): The scene `id` on `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `isScene` (function): Whether `value` is a defined scene (an entry of kind `scene`), as a module exports it.
- `Scene` (type): A defined scene: its spec with defaults filled, plus `id` and `kind`.
- `SCENE_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `SceneAction` (type): A dev action of a scene: runs between steps inside `w.run`, with plain-data `args`; recorded in replays.
- `SceneOptions` (interface): How a scene starts.
- `SceneRun` (interface): A started scene: the scene, its world and its settings store.
- `SceneSpec` (interface): How a scene is written: `defineScene(id, spec)`.
- `Session` (interface): A started scene that records its inputs from step 0, so `record()` returns it as a replay.
- `startScene` (function): Starts a scene (an id on the registry, or a scene): a new settings store with the scene's settings and then `options.settings` over the defaults, a world seeded with `options.seed`, the scene's `step` as the system `scene`, then its `setup`.

### [`engine/sim/state.ts`](../engine/sim/state.ts)

- `AnyComponents` (type): The components of an untyped world: any declared kind, by name.
- `ComponentData` (type): One component's data: its fields by name, plain data (numbers, strings, booleans, null, arrays, plain objects).
- `ComponentKind` (interface): A component kind as `defineComponent` stores it in the registry.
- `ComponentOf` (type): The data type of a component of kind fields `S`, as `make` returns it: writable, defaults filled.
- `componentTable` (function): The component table of `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `ComponentTable` (interface): A registry's component kinds, read once each: their field lists and validated new values.
- `defineComponent` (function): Declares a component kind on `registry` (the shared one by default): `name` is the entity property that holds it, `fields` its schema.
- `diffStates` (function): Where two states part, field by field, at most `limit` differences: entities are matched by id (`entities.7` for an entity on one side only, `entities.7.position.x` for a field), the rest by key and index.
- `Entity` (type): An entity: its id and the components it holds, by kind name (`e.position`).
- `EntityData` (interface): An entity as plain data: its id and its components by kind name.
- `hashState` (function): The digest of a state as 16 hex digits: what `world.hash()` returns.
- `PhysicsHook` (interface): The physics part of the world's state, hashed and captured with the rest (WP 3.1 plugs Rapier in; §6.5 items 5–7).
- `SpawnSpec` (type): What `spawn` takes: components by kind name, each with any of its fields (the rest take their defaults).
- `STATE_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `STATE_FORMAT` (const): The hash format; changing what the hash reads changes this tag, and with it every golden.
- `StateDifference` (interface): Where two states part: the path (`entities.7.position.x`) and each side's value (undefined when absent).
- `StateView` (interface): What the hash reads, live or stored: the ids, entities (in id order), timers, settings, RNG states and the physics hook's state.
- `traceState` (function): The per-part and per-entity digests of a state (the `hash` field is `hashState`'s; `live` as there).
- `With` (type): An entity known to hold the components `K` (what `query` returns).
- `WorldState` (interface): The sim as plain data: what `world.state()` returns and the hash covers.
- `WorldTrace` (interface): Per-part and per-entity digests, so a mismatch names the part and the entity (PLAN.md §6.5 item 6).

### [`engine/sim/systems.ts`](../engine/sim/systems.ts)

- `createSystems` (function): Makes an empty schedule.
- `Intents` (re-export): What the sim reads from outside in one step, recorded by replays (the vocabulary: engine/input/intents.ts).
- `Phase` (type): A phase of the step.
- `phaseIndex` (function): The place of `phase` in the step (`timers` sits just before `rules`).
- `PHASES` (const): The phases systems run in, in order; the engine's `timers` stage runs between `readback` and `rules`.
- `STEP_ORDER` (const): One step, in order: the phases, the engine's stages (`timers`, `spawns`, `despawns`, `events`) among them.
- `System` (interface): A system in the schedule.
- `SYSTEM_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `SystemFn` (type): A system: called once per step with the world and the step's intents.
- `Systems` (interface): A world's systems, in run order.
- `SystemSpec` (interface): A system as `createWorld({ systems })` takes it: the phase is `rules` when left out.

### [`engine/sim/world.ts`](../engine/sim/world.ts)

- `createWorld` (function): Makes a world.
- `SimRng` (interface): Sim RNG streams: `rng('ai')`, and `rng.entity(id, 'anim')` for an entity's own (dropped when it despawns).
- `SystemProbe` (type): A probe around each system's run (the stats meter's, engine/dev/stats.ts): the system's name and phase, and its run, to call once.
- `World` (interface): The sim world: entities, components, systems, events, RNG, timers, state, hash, capture and restore.
- `WORLD_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `WorldEvents` (type): The listeners a world offers game code: `on`, `once`, `off`, scopes and the trace; events go through `w.emit`.
- `WorldOptions` (interface): How a world is made.
- `WorldTimers` (type): The timers a world offers game code: `after` and `every` in sim seconds; the world steps them.

### [`engine/ui/chrome.ts`](../engine/ui/chrome.ts)

- `Chrome` (interface): The page's touch-mode chrome.
- `createChrome` (function): Makes the touch-mode chrome of `document` (off until `setTouch(true)`).
- `TURN_HINT` (const): The hint shown to a phone held upright.

### [`engine/ui/labels.ts`](../engine/ui/labels.ts)

- `Anchor` (type): Where a label is: a point read every frame (a `Vector3` the caller moves follows), or a function giving one.
- `createWorldLayer` (function): Builds the world layer: labels in `labels`, damage numbers in `numbers` (two sibling layers, numbers on top).
- `DAMAGE_NUMBERS` (const): The damage numbers' behaviour (see the file comment); seconds and metres.
- `DamageColumn` (interface): The last damage number's column: its anchor (m), when its latest number came (s) and how many it holds.
- `DamageOptions` (interface): How a damage number is shown.
- `damageRise` (function): How far above its anchor a damage number is `age` seconds after it appeared, m.
- `Label` (interface): A world-anchored label: change its text, anchor or visibility at any time; it shows them at the next frame.
- `LABEL_CODES` (const): The error codes of the world-anchored elements.
- `LabelOptions` (interface): How a label is made.
- `OverlayCamera` (interface): What the overlay reads of a camera: any three.js camera (without `near` and `far`, it culls only behind it).
- `projectToOverlay` (function): Where the point (x, y, z) shows on an overlay `width` × `height` CSS px over `camera`'s picture: writes its centre (px from the top left) and its depth (m in front of the camera) into `out`, or returns false, writing nothing, when it is nearer than `near` or beyond `far`.
- `stackDamage` (function): Where a damage number at `point` goes at `time` (s), after the column `last`: in it when near enough and soon enough (`last` is then updated), else in a new column at `point`.
- `WorldFrame` (interface): What one frame places by.
- `WorldLayer` (interface): The labels and damage numbers of one overlay.
- `worldPoint` (function): `point` as `[x, y, z]`, or `UI_BAD_POINT` naming `what`.
- `WorldPoint` (type): A point in the world, m: three.js's `Vector3`, `{ x, y, z }` or `[x, y, z]` (physics' `Vec3Like`).

### [`engine/ui/overlay.ts`](../engine/ui/overlay.ts)

- `createOverlay` (function): Builds the overlay over `options.canvas` (see the file comment).
- `HUD_PLACES` (const): Every HUD place, in the order the overlay adds them.
- `HudOptions` (interface): How a HUD line is shown.
- `HudPlace` (type): Where a HUD line goes: a corner, or the middle of the top or bottom edge.
- `Overlay` (interface): The overlay over one canvas (see the file comment).
- `OVERLAY_CODES` (const): The error codes of the overlay.
- `OverlayOptions` (interface): How an overlay is made.

### [`engine/ui/state.ts`](../engine/ui/state.ts)

- `UiElementState` (interface): One overlay element (see the file comment).
- `uiState` (function): The overlay under `root` as plain data (see the file comment).
- `UiState` (interface): The overlay as plain data (see the file comment).

### [`engine/ui/swipe.ts`](../engine/ui/swipe.ts)

- `attachSwipes` (function): Lets fingers swipe away the `[data-swipe]` elements of `document` (see the file comment).
- `SWIPE_DISTANCE` (const): A swipe this far (CSS px) dismisses.
- `SWIPE_FLICK` (const): A flick this far (CSS px) …
- `SWIPE_FLICK_TIME` (const): … within this long (s) dismisses too.
- `SWIPE_FLY` (const): A dismissed element flies this much further (CSS px) …
- `SWIPE_FLY_TIME` (const): … over this long (s).
- `Swipes` (interface): Swiping on a page.

### [`engine/ui/touch.ts`](../engine/ui/touch.ts)

- `createTouchLayer` (function): Builds the layer for `layout` (null: only the stick) and appends it to `document.body`.
- `defineTouchLayout` (function): Registers a touch layout (on the shared registry by default).
- `getTouchLayout` (function): The touch layout `id`.
- `TOUCH_SLOTS` (const): The button slots, in fill order (see the file comment).
- `TouchButtonSpec` (interface): One button of a touch layout.
- `TouchLayer` (interface): The touch controls' layer in a page.
- `TouchLayerState` (interface): What the layer shows this frame.
- `TouchLayout` (type): A touch layout entry.
- `touchLayoutKind` (function): Declares the kind `touchlayout` on `registry` unless it has it.
- `TouchLayoutSpec` (interface): How a touch layout is written.
- `touchScale` (function): The scale of the touch controls for a screen `width` × `height` CSS px: `--touch-k`.
- `TouchSlot` (interface): Where a button sits: its centre's distance from the right and bottom edges, and its diameter, in k CSS px.

### [`engine/world/ai.ts`](../engine/world/ai.ts)

- `ATTACK_TOKENS` (const): Attack tokens with every field at its default: 3 tokens, none held.
- `ATTACK_TOKENS_FIELDS` (const): The attack tokens' fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('tokens', { description, fields: … })`.
- `AttackTokens` (interface): Attack tokens: who holds one and when the next may be granted (`ATTACK_TOKENS_FIELDS` says what each means).
- `canSee` (function): Whether an agent with its feet at `from` is aware of a target with its feet at `to`: within `range` metres on the ground, and either within `near` metres or in a clear sight line from its eye to the target's `aim`.
- `clearSight` (function): Whether the straight line from (ax, ay, az) to (bx, by, bz) metres passes over every tile it crosses (walked in order, as Amanatides and Woo's grid traversal does): no tile's top (`level.top`) stands above the line's lowest point over that tile, and no point of it lies off the map.
- `holdsToken` (function): Whether `id` holds a token: one of the oldest `cap` grants.
- `keepTokens` (function): Keeps the tokens of the holders `keep` approves (alive, still attacking), freeing the rest: how many are held.
- `releaseToken` (function): Gives `id`'s token back (its attack ended, or was broken off): true when it held one.
- `SIGHT` (const): `canSee`'s defaults: emberdeep's 150 units of sight and 60 of sense, an eye at 1.5 m on a chest at 1 m.
- `SightOptions` (interface): How `canSee` looks.
- `takeToken` (function): Asks for a token for `id` at sim time `time` (s): true when it holds one now.

### [`engine/world/level/colliders.ts`](../engine/world/level/colliders.ts)

- `groundSlab` (function): The slab under the whole level, one tile wider than the map all round, from 1 m down to y 0.
- `levelColliders` (function): The colliders of every glyph with a collider recipe, by glyph id: merged boxes, hulls under `slopes`, cylinders.
- `Slopes` (interface): The level's ramps and daises (engine/world/level/shapes.ts), which the hull colliders stand under.

### [`engine/world/level/compile.ts`](../engine/world/level/compile.ts)

- `compileLevel` (function): Compiles a level's text against the legend of `options.registry` (the shared one by default) into plain data; see the file comment.
- `CompileOptions` (interface): What `compileLevel` takes beside the text.
- `levelName` (function): The name of a level file: `fixtures/levels/room.txt` → `room`.

### [`engine/world/level/glyph.ts`](../engine/world/level/glyph.ts)

- `defineGlyph` (function): Defines a glyph on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `Glyph` (type): A `glyph` entry: what one map character means.
- `GLYPH_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `glyph` entry.
- `glyphKind` (function): Declares the kind `glyph` on `registry`, with the engine's v1 and v2 glyphs, unless it has it.
- `GlyphSpec` (type): What `defineGlyph` takes: `char`, and any other field (`nav` may give one flag, the other keeping its default).
- `legendOf` (function): Every glyph of `registry` (the shared one by default), keyed by its character, in id order.

### [`engine/world/level/grid.ts`](../engine/world/level/grid.ts)

- `byText` (const): Code-unit order, so sorting never depends on the locale.
- `glyphsOf` (function): The distinct glyphs of `grid`, by id.
- `holds` (function): A predicate: whether tile (col, row) of `grid` holds one of `glyphs`.
- `TileGrid` (interface): A level's grid: its size, its tile size (m) and each tile's glyph, row-major.

### [`engine/world/level/heights.ts`](../engine/world/level/heights.ts)

- `floorHeight` (function): The walkable surface's height (m) at (x, z): the highest flat floor, ramp or dais there; 0 outside the map.
- `HeightSource` (type): What the height queries read: a compiled level, or validate.ts's view of one before it compiles.
- `solidAt` (function): Whether (x, z) is in a solid tile (a wall, a pillar, a low wall, a brazier), or outside the map.
- `surfaceAt` (function): The surface tag underfoot at (x, z): a dais's where it stands highest, else its tile's glyph's; '' outside the map.
- `tileAt` (function): The tile under (x, z) metres, or null outside the map.
- `topHeight` (function): The top (m) of whatever stands at (x, z): a wall's top over its tiles, a brazier's within its radius, the floor elsewhere; 0 outside the map.

### [`engine/world/level/legend.ts`](../engine/world/level/legend.ts)

- `V1_GLYPHS` (const): The v1 glyphs by id, as `defineGlyph` specs (the kind's defaults fill the rest).
- `V2_GLYPHS` (const): The v2 glyphs by id (WP 4.2): the hall's gallery, stairs, dais and brazier.

### [`engine/world/level/level.ts`](../engine/world/level/level.ts)

- `defineLevel` (function): Registers a level on `registry` (the shared one by default) after checking its text compiles against that registry's legend; returns the entry.
- `getLevel` (function): The level `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default), compiled: its name is the id without `level:`.
- `LEVEL_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `level` entry.
- `LevelEntry` (type): A `level` entry: a level's text and where it came from.

### [`engine/world/level/meshes.ts`](../engine/world/level/meshes.ts)

- `levelMeshes` (function): The mesh descriptors: one per recipe, bottom, top, surface and footprint, for every glyph whose mesh is not 'none'.

### [`engine/world/level/parse.ts`](../engine/world/level/parse.ts)

- `LevelHeader` (interface): The front matter's values, defaults filled.
- `ParsedLevel` (interface): A level's text, read: header, map rows (each an array of characters), positions and problems.
- `parseLevel` (function): Reads a level's text: its front matter, its map rows and their positions, and the problems of the text itself.

### [`engine/world/level/problems.ts`](../engine/world/level/problems.ts)

- `LEVEL_CODES` (const): The level codes, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `LevelCode` (type): A level code.
- `levelProblem` (function): A problem with `code` at `line`:`column`, its message filled from `values` (which name `at`).
- `LevelProblem` (interface): One problem with a level: its code, where it is (from 1, in the whole file) and the sentence naming its fix.
- `where` (const): `<file>:<line>:<column>`, the `at` of a problem's message.

### [`engine/world/level/rects.ts`](../engine/world/level/rects.ts)

- `findBlocks` (function): The 4-connected blocks of the tiles `inside` accepts, and the block index of every tile (−1 outside any).
- `mergeRects` (function): Rectangles `[col0, row0, col1, row1]` (inclusive) covering every tile of a cols × rows grid that `inside` accepts.
- `TileBlock` (interface): A 4-connected block of tiles: its first tile in reading order, its bounding rectangle and its tile count.

### [`engine/world/level/shapes.ts`](../engine/world/level/shapes.ts)

- `daisHeight` (function): A dais's surface height (m) at (x, z), or −Infinity off its base.
- `findDaises` (function): The daises of `grid` and the dais blocks that make none.
- `findRamps` (function): The ramps of `grid` and the ramp blocks that make none.
- `frustumPoints` (function): The corners of a dais's hull (m): its base octagon on the ground (and at its bottom, when above 0) and its top.
- `octagonRadius` (function): An octagon's "radius" at an offset from its centre: the distance to its nearest face (faces toward the axes and the diagonals).
- `rampHeight` (function): A ramp's surface height (m) at (x, z), on tiles `tile` metres wide; held to its edges' heights past them.
- `ShapeProblem` (interface): A block of a ramp or dais glyph that makes no ramp or dais, and why, for validate.ts.
- `wedgePoints` (function): The corners of a ramp's hull (m): its rectangle on the ground, and over each corner its height there when above 0.

### [`engine/world/level/types.ts`](../engine/world/level/types.ts)

- `BoxCollider` (interface): An axis-aligned box collider (Rapier's cuboid: half extents `(max − min)/2`, centred at `(min + max)/2`).
- `ColliderDescriptor` (type): A collider descriptor: a merged box, a hull or a cylinder, by `shape`.
- `CompiledLevel` (interface): A compiled level: the map, its legend, per-tile grids and descriptors; see the file comment.
- `CylinderCollider` (interface): An upright cylinder collider (Rapier's cylinder, three.js's CylinderGeometry): one per tile, at its centre.
- `DaisDescriptor` (interface): A dais: an octagonal frustum (faces toward the axes and the diagonals) standing on a block of a dais glyph's tiles.
- `GroundDescriptor` (interface): The slab under the whole level: the ground's collider, one tile wider than the map all round, 1 m deep.
- `HullCollider` (interface): A convex hull collider (Rapier's convex hull of its points): a ramp's wedge or a dais's frustum, from the ground.
- `LEVEL_FORMAT` (const): The format tag of a compiled level.
- `LevelGlyph` (interface): One glyph as the level used it: the `glyph` entry's fields (engine/world/level/glyph.ts) and its id.
- `LightSpot` (interface): A light spot: a tile's centre, `lightHeight` above its top.
- `MeshDescriptor` (interface): What the level meshes (WP 2.4) build for one recipe at one height: the tiles, merged and as pieces.
- `Point3` (type): A point in metres: `[x, y, z]`.
- `RampDescriptor` (interface): A ramp: a filled rectangle of a ramp glyph's tiles (stairs) whose floor rises in a straight slope from `bottom` along the side opposite `rises` to `top` along `rises`, the side whose neighbours stand at its top (a gallery).
- `Side` (type): A compass side of a block: north is −Z (row 0's edge), south +Z, west −X, east +X.
- `SpawnPoint` (interface): A spawn point: a tile's centre, on its floor.
- `TileRect` (type): A rectangle of tiles, inclusive: `[col0, row0, col1, row1]`.

### [`engine/world/level/validate.ts`](../engine/world/level/validate.ts)

- `CheckedLevel` (interface): A level read against its legend: the parsed text, the glyph of every tile, its slopes, and the structural problems.
- `checkLevel` (function): The structural problems of a level's text: the text's own, unknown characters and bad footprint blocks.
- `LevelSource` (interface): Where a level comes from, for messages, and the legend to read it with.
- `NAV_CLIMB` (const): The default climb limit between neighbouring tiles' floors (m): the prototype's `CLIMB`, 3.5 units.
- `validateLevel` (function): Every problem of a level's text, structural and content (see the file comment), in a fixed order; `[]` when it is fine.

### [`engine/world/level/walk.ts`](../engine/world/level/walk.ts)

- `canStep` (function): Whether a body walks from the centre of tile (col, row) to the centre of tile (col + dc, row + dr), climbing at most `climb` metres between samples.
- `STEP_SAMPLES` (const): How many points along a step `canStep` samples the floor at.
- `WalkArea` (interface): An area of tiles that reach each other both ways: its first tile in reading order and its tile count.
- `walkAreas` (function): The areas of `level`'s walkable tiles under the climb limit, and the area index of every tile (−1 if unwalkable).

### [`engine/world/nav.ts`](../engine/world/nav.ts)

- `FlowField` (class): Every tile's walking distance to a goal set: walk downhill to get there.
- `FlowOptions` (interface): What `flowField` takes.
- `GroundPoint` (type): A point on the ground (m): x east, z south.
- `LOOK_AHEAD` (const): How many tiles downhill `FlowField.direction` looks ahead (shardfall's 3).
- `NAV_DIRECTIONS` (const): The 8 neighbours, as [columns east, rows south]: east, west, south, north, then the diagonals (bit k of a step).
- `NAV_GRID_FIELDS` (const): The options of `new NavGrid(level, options)`.
- `NavGrid` (class): The walkable grid of a compiled level, and the searches over it (see the file comment).
- `NavGridOptions` (type): What `new NavGrid` takes: each field of `NAV_GRID_FIELDS`, optional.
- `NEAREST_RINGS` (const): How many rings of tiles `nearestOpen` searches round a blocked point (shardfall's 5).

### [`engine/world/props/catalog.ts`](../engine/world/props/catalog.ts)

- `BUILT_IN_PROPS` (const): The engine's props, by id.

### [`engine/world/props/place.ts`](../engine/world/props/place.ts)

- `levelProps` (function): The placements `level` makes for the props of `registry` (the shared one by default); see the file comment.
- `propBody` (function): The body `physics.addBody` takes for `placement`, or `null` when its prop has none; see the file comment.
- `PropBody` (interface): A prop's body, as `physics.addBody` takes it (engine/physics/world.ts's `BodySpec`).
- `PropCollider` (type): A prop's collider, as `physics.addBody` takes it.
- `PropPlacement` (interface): A prop placed: which, its base (m) and its turn about +Y (rad).
- `propPose` (function): Where `placement` is drawn while no body moves it: the prop's centre and turn.
- `PropPose` (interface): Where a prop is drawn: its centre (m) and its turn, `[x, y, z, w]`.

### [`engine/world/props/prop.ts`](../engine/world/props/prop.ts)

- `defineProp` (function): Defines a prop on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `getProp` (function): The prop `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); a missing id gives `prop:crate`, with a warning.
- `Prop` (type): A `prop` entry: see the file comment.
- `PROP_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `prop` entry.
- `PROP_PART_FIELDS` (const): The fields of one part: a mesh of the prop.
- `PROP_SHAPES` (const): The physics shapes a prop's body may have, sized as three.js sizes its geometries.
- `propCentre` (function): The height of a prop's centre above its base (m): its body's origin, half its shape's height; 0 without a body.
- `PropDefinition` (type): What `defineProp` takes: any field, and of its objects (body, light, place, each part and its flame) any key.
- `propKind` (function): Declares the kind `prop` on `registry`, with the engine's props, unless it has it.
- `PropKnock` (interface): How hard a knock is, as engine/physics/bodies.ts's `knock` takes it.
- `PropPart` (type): One part of a `prop` entry, filled: see `PROP_PART_FIELDS`.
- `PropTouch` (interface): What a hook is given: the prop, its body, where the touch comes from, and the means to answer it.

### [`engine/world/spatial.ts`](../engine/world/spatial.ts)

- `SPATIAL_HASH_FIELDS` (const): The options of `new SpatialHash(options)`.
- `SpatialHash` (class): Points on the ground, hashed by cell (see the file comment).
- `SpatialHashOptions` (type): What `new SpatialHash` takes: each field of `SPATIAL_HASH_FIELDS`, optional.

### [`engine/world/steer.ts`](../engine/world/steer.ts)

- `airTime` (function): How long (s) a body thrown up at `up` m/s flies under `gravity` (m/s², above 0) until it comes down to `rise` metres above where it left (below for a drop): the later root of `rise = up·t − gravity·t²/2`.
- `APPROACH_RING` (const): `approachRing`'s defaults: the prototype's walker (3 units either side, back at half speed, round at 0.4).
- `approachRing` (function): The way to wait round `to` on a ring of `ring.radius` metres: beyond `radius + band`, in by `followFlow` (straight when `field` is null); inside `radius − band`, straight out at `backoff` of full speed; on the ring, round it at `circle × sway` of full speed (`sway` in [−1, 1]; positive turns about +Y, anticlockwise seen from above).
- `ApproachRingOptions` (interface): What `approachRing` takes: the ring's radius, and how an agent moves in, out and round.
- `FOLLOW` (const): `followFlow`'s defaults: straight within 4 m in a clear line (emberdeep's 64 units), full speed to the target.
- `followFlow` (function): The way to walk from `from` to `to` along `field` (a flow field toward the target's tile): straight at `to` within `near` metres when the grid has a clear line for a body (`NavGrid.lineOfSight`), else the field's look-ahead direction (`FlowField.direction`), else, where the field has no way (beyond its reach, or arrived at the goal tile's centre), straight at `to`, as the prototype does.
- `FollowOptions` (interface): How `followFlow` steers.
- `hop` (function): The launch velocity (m/s) that carries a body thrown up at `up` m/s from `from` to land on `to` under `gravity` (m/s²): `up` vertically and the ground distance over `airTime` across, so a jumper hops onto a crate as well as across the floor.
- `HOP` (const): The prototype slime's jumps: `up` (m/s) for a hop of at most `reach` metres, `pounce` (m/s) for its lower, flatter leap at a target.
- `hover` (function): A flyer's vertical speed (m/s) that holds its feet at `y` metres `height` over `floor`, bobbing `bob` metres at `bobRate` radians per second of `time` (s; its own clock, or the sim's plus a phase): the gap times `climb`.
- `HOVER` (const): `hover`'s defaults: the prototype's wisp, 20 units over the floor bobbing ±3 at 2 rad/s, climbing at 6 × the gap.
- `HoverOptions` (interface): How `hover` holds a flyer up.
- `seek` (function): The way from `from` to `to` on the ground: a unit vector, zero within a millimetre.
- `SteerPoint` (type): A point in the world (m): x east, y up, z south.

### [`eslint.config.js`](../eslint.config.js)

- `configure` (function): Builds the whole config; `switches` defaults to `SWITCHES` (tests turn every switch on).
- `default` (default): ESLint's settings for T0 (PLAN.md §6.10; `npm run lint`, inside `npm run check`): typescript-eslint's recommended rules without type information (so T0 stays fast), the file-comment and size rules, then the doctrine's rule families from tools/eslint/, one block per family, each message naming the fix.
- `SWITCHES` (const): Rules written ahead of the code they guard.

- `HeroTuning` (interface): What a scene may tune of the hero: his walk, take-off and dash speeds, m/s.

- `SLIME` (const): The slime's numbers (see the file comment).

### [`labs/box/cast/walker.ts`](../labs/box/cast/walker.ts)

- `levelWith` (const): Whether a point at height `y` (m) is level with the hero.
- `makeWalker` (function): A new walker's own state, its speed and sway's phase drawn from `rng`, facing `yaw`.
- `steerWalker` (function): The velocity (m/s) the walker wants this step, into `out`, turning it toward where it goes (see the file comment).

### [`labs/box/cast/wisp.ts`](../labs/box/cast/wisp.ts)

- `CROWD_WISP` (const): The wisp's component: which way it circles, and its hover's clock.
