- `steerWisp` (function): The velocity (m/s) the wisp wants this step, into `out`, its clock advanced (see the file comment).
- `WISP` (const): The wisp's numbers (see the file comment).
- `WispData` (interface): The wisp's own state, beside its crowd agent.

### [`labs/box/scenes/crowd-100.ts`](../labs/box/scenes/crowd-100.ts)

- `crowd100` (const): The crowd at 100.
- `default` (default): The crowd at 100, Box 4 (PLAN.md §9.0, WP 5.7): the crowd scene (labs/box/scenes/crowd-1000.ts) with 100 walkers, slimes and wisps, in four steps of the queue: few enough to follow one by one, and the scene the Box 4 replays play (tests/replays/box-4-*.replay.json), so they run quickly in the rendering page too.

### [`labs/box/scenes/crowd-1000.ts`](../labs/box/scenes/crowd-1000.ts)

- `CROWD_GRID` (const): The crowd's walkable grid: the hall under a climb of 6 cm, what a crowd body manages (Rapier 0.21 steps a capsule up 7 cm and a ball 8.5 cm, measured in WP 5.2), so the stairs' gentle rise is walkable and their sides are not.
- `CROWD_MEMBER` (const): A member's crowd agent (engine/physics/crowd.ts): its body, its make and what the last readback saw.
- `CROWD_SETTINGS` (const): The crowd's settings: how many, and the mix.
- `CROWD_TILES` (const): The tiles a member may start on: the hall's open floor, at height 0 (no dais, stairs or gallery).
- `crowd1000` (const): The crowd at 1,000.
- `CrowdComponents` (type): The scene's components.
- `default` (default): The crowd, Box 4 (PLAN.md §9.0, WP 5.7): the hall with a hero (labs/box/scenes/hall.ts) filling with `box.crowd.count` walkers, slimes and wisps (labs/box/cast/{walker,slime,wisp}.ts) that chase him, round the walls and pillars and up the stairs after him.
- `MIXES` (const): A crowd mix: the share of walkers, and of walkers and slimes together; the rest are wisps.
- `setupCrowd` (function): The crowd's setup: the hall and its hero, `box.crowd.count` members queued, the crowd's systems; the hero's id.
- `SPAWN` (const): Where members start: at least `away` m from the hero (the prototype's 80 units), `tries` draws, `jitter` in a tile.

### [`labs/box/scenes/crowd-5000.ts`](../labs/box/scenes/crowd-5000.ts)

- `crowd5000` (const): The crowd at 5,000.
- `default` (default): The crowd at 5,000, Box 4 (PLAN.md §9.0, WP 5.7): the crowd scene (labs/box/scenes/crowd-1000.ts) with 5,000 walkers, slimes and wisps, 25 entering a step, so the hall fills over 200 steps: the top of the perf ladder, and the page that shows the crowd grows to 5,000 with no pipeline built (tests/e2e/box-crowd.spec.ts).

### [`labs/box/scenes/hall-props.ts`](../labs/box/scenes/hall-props.ts)

- `default` (default): The hall with its props, Box 3 (PLAN.md §9.0, WP 4.6): the hall with a hero (labs/box/scenes/hall.ts) and its props, standing in the scene through `spawnProp` (their bodies in the physics world, the page drawing them through the instanced prop meshes): the level's own, a brazier's fire on each of its 30 stands (`levelProps`), and `box.hallProps.count` crates and barrels, 10 to 300, on the first of `HALL_SPOTS`.
- `HALL_PROPS_SETTINGS` (const): The scene's settings: how many crates and barrels.
- `HALL_SPOTS` (const): The 300 spots of the hall's crates and barrels (see the file comment), as placements on the floor or a stack.
- `HALL_SWING` (const): The scene's own component: the hero's shove, whose it is and its ticks left.
- `hallProps` (const): The hall with its props.
- `inShove` (function): Whether a shove from `hero` (his feet and heading) reaches the prop centred at `p` (see `SHOVE`).

- `SetFiles` (type): A set's directory as text: file name → contents.
- `SETS_DIR` (const): The sets' directory, `data/anim/sets/`: one directory per set, named by `setDirName`.

- `tagAlternates` (function): The set with `alt` added last to the tags of each clip made from another set's clip (one with an `orig`).
- `writeSetDir` (function): Writes a set's files into `dir`, made if missing, and removes the files it no longer has; lists what changed.

- `SHARDFALL_CATALOGS` (const): The catalogs that come from shardfall (its `anim/catalogs/`), by file name: 100STYLE's seven and Quaternius v2's.
- `SHARDFALL_SETS` (const): The sets that come from shardfall, by directory: each one's file in shardfall at `fa2dab6`.

- `shardfallSet` (function): The set in `dir` as this library keeps it, from the shardfall checkout and, for a set in `V1_SETS`, the my-3d2dge checkout (throws without it, naming the fix).
- `shardfallSetFiles` (function): The files of every set in `SHARDFALL_SETS`, by directory, as the repacker writes them.
- `V1_KEPT` (const): The clips a set keeps from my-3d2dge's v1 of it, by directory: those shardfall's version dropped.
- `V1_SETS` (const): The set of my-3d2dge whose `body` and `V1_KEPT` clips a shardfall set takes, by directory.

### [`tools/checkAll.ts`](../tools/checkAll.ts)

- `CACHE_DIRS` (const): The cache directories ESLint and Prettier create on a cold run.
- `CHECK_TOOLS` (const): The T0 tools, in the order their output is printed; `tsc` runs package.json's `typecheck` command.
- `checkAll` (function): Runs every tool in parallel, prints their output in order, and returns the exit code (0 only if all pass).
- `CheckTool` (interface): One T0 tool: its name and its command line, run from the repository root.

### [`tools/cmd/audio.ts`](../tools/cmd/audio.ts)

- `default` (default): Renders a sound in Node and prints its numbers, or mixes a replay's sound events (PLAN.md §8.1, WP 9.4, I-23).
- `encodeWav` (function): Encodes samples as a 16-bit mono PCM WAV file, clamped to ±1.
- `mixSoundEvents` (function): The events' effects rendered (each once per variant, seed 0, at 44,100 Hz) and summed into one mono mix at least `seconds` long, with each event's span in it, `[start, end)` in samples.
- `Picture` (type): A picture as RGBA bytes, row by row from the top.
- `replaySoundEvents` (function): Plays `replay` (its scene defined on `registry`) step by step, as `playReplay` does, hashing its checkpoints, and reads the sound events from the sim's event trace after setup, each change-point and each step.
- `SoundEvent` (interface): One sound event of a replay: when, from which sim event, which effect at which gain and variant.
- `SoundTimeline` (interface): A replay's sound events, the problems of those that name no sound, its length and the hashes of its checkpoints.
- `spectrogram` (function): A spectrogram of `samples` as RGBA bytes (see the file comment for its axes and colours).
- `SPECTROGRAM` (const): The spectrogram's size, FFT length, floor (dBFS) and lowest frequency (Hz).

### [`tools/cmd/check.ts`](../tools/cmd/check.ts)

- `assetScan` (const): The asset scan (doctrine: Assets).
- `binaryKind` (function): What binary format `bytes` (a file named `path`) is, or undefined for text.
- `CheckContext` (interface): What a plugin is given: the repository root, and whether this checkout is an ultracode lane.
- `CheckOutcome` (interface): What a plugin found.
- `CheckPlugin` (interface): One repository check.
- `default` (default): Runs the repository checks no standard tool covers, last in `npm run check` (PLAN.md §8.1).
- `discoverPlugins` (function): The plugins: the asset scan, then each `check` exported by a module in `tools/cmd/` (a text scan finds them).
- `isLane` (function): Whether `root` is an ultracode lane: `X_LANE` when set (0 or 1), else whether it is a linked git worktree.
- `repositoryFiles` (function): The files git tracks or would track under `root`: tracked plus untracked, ignored ones left out.
- `runChecks` (function): Runs `plugins` side by side and merges what they found; in a lane, `warnInLane` plugins only warn.

### [`tools/cmd/ci.ts`](../tools/cmd/ci.ts)

- `CI_OUT` (const): Where `x ci --local` writes, relative to the root.
- `CI_STEPS` (const): The steps of `x ci --local`, in order (PLAN.md §8.9).
- `CiDeps` (interface): What `x ci` reaches outside itself; the tests replace each part.
- `CiRun` (interface): A whole run of the gate.
- `CiStep` (interface): One step of the gate.
- `createCiCommand` (function): Builds the `x ci` command; the tests pass fakes for the step runner, git, the selections and the clock.
- `default` (default): The merge gate (PLAN.md §8.9, WP 0.9): `x ci --local` runs `CI_STEPS` in order on this machine, holds the tiers to their budgets (tools/lib/tiers.ts), writes `out/ci/summary.md` and, when everything passed, records HEAD in `out/ci/last-green`, the base of the selections until main holds a gate.
- `Head` (interface): HEAD's commit and branch, and the uncommitted changes (`git status --porcelain` lines).
- `KEPT_CACHES` (const): What `npm ci` must not wipe, relative to the root: the tools' caches, and Vitest's record of each file's duration, from which it starts the longest files first (without it, T1 took 39 s instead of 36 s).
- `readHead` (function): Reads `Head` with git.
- `readT2Full` (function): The duration of the last full T2 run that passed, if one was recorded.
- `renderSummary` (function): The run as Markdown, for `out/ci/summary.md` (and the GitHub workflow's step summary).
- `runCi` (function): Runs the gate in `root`: every step, the budgets, the summary and, when green, `out/ci/last-green`.
- `spawnStep` (const): Runs `command` as a child process, stdout and stderr captured together, colours off.
- `StepOutcome` (interface): What running one command gave: its exit code (1 when it could not start), its wall time and its output.
- `StepResult` (interface): One step's result.
- `StepRunner` (type): Runs one command from `cwd`; the tests inject a fake.
- `toResult` (function): The run as the dispatcher's result: the timing table, the T2 selection and one finding per problem.

### [`tools/cmd/deps.ts`](../tools/cmd/deps.ts)

- `check` (const): The `deps` plugin of `x check` (T0): the offline check.
- `createDepsCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests inject the day, the active node, a fixture registry and a recording runner.
- `default` (default): Checks the dependency pins against `tools/deps.json` (offline), and asks the registry for compatible releases to adopt and for lines that have qualified (PLAN.md §6.10; doctrine: Mastery, Common ground).

### [`tools/cmd/describe.ts`](../tools/cmd/describe.ts)

- `createDescribeCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests shorten the child process's time limit.
- `default` (default): Lists the registries from their schemas (PLAN.md §8.1, §6.6): `x describe` names every kind with its entry count, `x describe <kind>` gives its fields (type, default, range, unit, docs) and ids, and `x describe <kind> <id>` one entry's values, `*` marking those that differ from the default.
- `describeFile` (function): Where `x describe [kind [id]]` writes the whole description: `describe.json` beside its report.
- `describeInWorker` (function): Runs the listing in a child Node process over `root`'s registrations; resolves to what it sent, or to the failure when it hung (stopped after `timeoutMs`) or ended without a listing, naming the module it was loading.
- `fieldLine` (function): One line for a field: name, type, default, range, unit, values, flags, then its description.
- `idsLine` (function): A kind's ids as one line of at most `IDS_LINE` characters; a cut list says how many there are and where.
- `listing` (function): What one listing prints, from the shared registry; throws the registry's error for an unknown kind or id.
- `Listing` (interface): What one listing prints, besides the verdict, and the data `describe.json` holds.
- `loadRegistrations` (function): Imports each module that registers content, telling `loading` first; a module that fails becomes a warning.
- `registersContent` (function): Whether a parsed module calls something that registers content (comments, strings and declarations aside).
- `REGISTRATION_ROOTS` (const): Where modules that register content live.
- `registrationModules` (function): The modules under `root` that register content, repository-relative and sorted.
- `WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS` (const): How long the child process may take before it is stopped and the module it was loading named (ms).
- `WorkerDone` (interface): What the child process reports when it is done: what loaded, and the listing or the usage problem.
- `WorkerMessage` (type): One message from the child process: the module it starts loading, or the end.

### [`tools/cmd/docs.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.ts)

- `check` (const): The `x check` plugin: the drift checks without the examples (they run in T1 and in `x docs --check`).
- `checkComments` (function): What the code says about its own documentation: missing or long file comments, undocumented exports, bad codes.
- `createDocsCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests inject the source checkouts and the planned paths.
- `default` (default): Generates and checks the docs that come from the code (PLAN.md §6.8, §8.12): `docs/INDEX.md`, `docs/API.md` and `docs/ERRORS.md`, the `@example` blocks, the paths the docs mention, and `docs/PROGRESS.md`'s length.
- `DocsOptions` (type): Options for the checks; tests inject the source checkouts and the planned paths.
- `driftChecks` (function): Every drift check except the examples: comments, codes, paths, generated docs and PROGRESS.md.
- `MAX_COMMENT_LINES` (const): The longest a file comment (PLAN.md §6.8) or `docs/PROGRESS.md` (one screen) may run, in lines.
- `PROGRESS` (const): The one screen every session reads first: where things stand, what is next, the open issues.

### [`tools/cmd/dump.ts`](../tools/cmd/dump.ts)

- `default` (default): Dumps the scene and the state of the page `x inspect` keeps open, as text (PLAN.md §8.1, §8.3, WP 2.7): `__engine.scene.dump()`, one object a line (name, type, position, size, material, triangles, entity), then the run's tick, hash and entities.

### [`tools/cmd/esc.ts`](../tools/cmd/esc.ts)

- `check` (const): The `esc` plugin of `x check` (T0): well-formed records, none overdue, a current README.
- `checkEscalations` (function): The `x check` rules: well-formed records with unique ids, no open record overdue, a current README.
- `createEscCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests inject the clock and the environment.
- `default` (default): Escalations and the calls made without an answer (DOCTRINE.md, Escalation; PLAN.md §8.14, ADR-0017): writes and lists the records in docs/escalations/ (tools/lib/escalations.ts), and checks them as `x check`'s `esc` plugin.
- `EscOptions` (interface): What the command reads from outside; tests pass a virtual clock and a fixed environment.
- `messageFor` (function): The short message `open` prints for the owner: the question, the options and what happens without an answer.
- `runId` (function): The run a record belongs to: `--run`, else `$X_RUN`, else the Claude Code session, else `local`.

### [`tools/cmd/eval.ts`](../tools/cmd/eval.ts)

- `default` (default): Evaluates JavaScript in the page `x inspect` keeps open, and prints its value as JSON (PLAN.md §8.1, WP 2.7): `node x eval "__engine.hash()"`.

### [`tools/cmd/film.ts`](../tools/cmd/film.ts)

- `addWorktree` (function): Checks commit `sha` out in a temporary worktree under out/film/, with this tree's node_modules linked into it.
- `default` (default): Films a page (PLAN.md WP 3.11, I-28): plays a script of steps over `__engine.input` and `step`, shoots a frame wherever the script says, lays the frames out on a labelled contact sheet, and with `--compare <ref>` films the same steps at that commit and attributes every pixel that differs to an object, through the ID pass.
- `FilmStep` (interface): One step of a film: the `__engine` member it calls and the arguments; the verb `shot` films a frame.
- `hasFile` (const): Whether commit `sha` has the file `path`.
- `parseSteps` (function): Reads a script of steps (see the file comment); throws `UsageError` naming the step it cannot read.
- `PARTS` (const): How many parts, each followed by a frame, a `step` is filmed in when the script never shoots.
- `removeWorktree` (function): Removes a worktree `addWorktree` made: the node_modules link first (never what it points at), then the checkout.
- `resolveRef` (function): The commit `ref` names, in full; throws `UsageError` when it names none.
- `sameSources` (const): Whether the working tree's sources are commit `sha`'s: no tracked change, no untracked file git does not ignore.
- `SHOT` (const): The shot a film takes: the pixels, the ID pass and the thumbnail, without the look metrics.
- `simSteps` (const): `n` sim steps with what the virtual device holds.

### [`tools/cmd/help.ts`](../tools/cmd/help.ts)

- `default` (default): Prints the generated help: every command, or one command's file comment and flags.

### [`tools/cmd/inspect.ts`](../tools/cmd/inspect.ts)

- `callSession` (function): Sends `op` with `body` to the session; resolves with its JSON reply, or rejects with its error's message.
- `default` (default): Keeps one headless page open over the Vite dev server, for `x eval`, `x dump` and `x set`, which `x shot` reuses while it runs (PLAN.md §8.1, WP 2.7; doctrine: Agent-operable).
- `findSession` (function): The running session's info, or null; a session whose process is gone is cleared.
- `Opened` (interface): A shot taken (for `x shot`), with what the page said: its signal, its failures so far and its console.
- `pageErrorFinding` (const): A page error as a failure.
- `pageFailures` (function): The failures of a page that should be ready: its thrown errors, its error signals, no signal, another backend.
- `reloadLines` (const): The line every reply starts with when Vite reloaded the page since the last one, else nothing.
- `SESSION_FILE` (const): Where a running session says where it listens.
- `SessionInfo` (interface): What `session.json` holds.
- `sessionShot` (function): The session's `shot` op: the open tab when it shows `path`, else a new tab of the browser opened on `path`.
- `SessionTab` (interface): What the session's `shot` op works with: its tab, the page open in it, its browser, Vite's URL and the root.
- `shootInSession` (function): Shoots `path` through the running inspect session (tools/cmd/inspect.ts): its page when it shows `path`, else a new tab of its browser; null when the page has no `__engine.shot` (then `x shot` screenshots it itself).

### [`tools/cmd/new.ts`](../tools/cmd/new.ts)

- `CheckName` (type): One check's name.
- `CHECKS` (const): The checks a kind may ask for.
- `default` (default): Scaffolds a new entry of a kind from its template (PLAN.md §8.13): `x new <kind> <id>` writes the files of `tools/templates/<kind>/`, filled in for the id, then runs the kind's checks and prints the summary.
- `fill` (function): Fills `{{id}}`, `{{name}}` and `{{dir}}` in `text`; throws on any other placeholder.
- `Kind` (interface): A kind, as its manifest declares it.
- `listKinds` (function): Reads and validates every kind under `tools/templates/`; throws naming the first problem.
- `NEXT` (const): What to do after writing an entry of a kind whose manifest has no `next`.
- `render` (function): The files an entry of `kind` with `id` consists of: repository path → formatted text.
- `runCheck` (function): Runs one check on the new files; returns one sentence per problem.
- `runChecks` (function): Runs a kind's checks on `files`: one line per check, and a finding per problem.
- `testKind` (function): Writes `kind`'s sample, checks it and removes it again.
- `writeFiles` (function): Writes rendered files; refuses (throws) when any exists.

### [`tools/cmd/perf.ts`](../tools/cmd/perf.ts)

- `agentsSetting` (function): The setting `asked` (`--agents`, else the budget's): an integer setting that allows the top rung's agents.
- `BUDGET_KEYS` (const): What a Node run and a ladder rung measure: milliseconds per step, per hash and per capture.
- `budgetPath` (function): A scene's budget file, repository-relative: `:` in the id becomes `-`.
- `default` (default): Performance as counters against budgets, never frames per second (PLAN.md §8.1, §8.7, WPs 1.5 and 5.5).
- `DEFAULT_STEPS` (const): The steps each way takes unless its budget section or `--steps` says otherwise.
- `LADDER` (const): The crowd ladder's rungs, in agents.
- `measure` (function): One run's timings: ms per step, then per hash and per capture of the state it reached (10 of each).
- `median` (function): The middle value (the mean of the two middle ones for an even count).
- `PAGE_KEYS` (const): What a page measures: `__engine.stats()`'s means, then its counts.
- `PageKey` (type): One quantity a page measures.
- `PerfBudget` (interface): A budget file, `tests/baselines/perf/<scene id>.json` (see the file comment).
- `PerfKey` (type): One quantity a Node run measures.
- `readBudget` (function): Reads and checks a budget file; throws `UsageError` naming each problem (an unknown key with the closest).
- `recordTrend` (function): Appends `measured` under `key` to the trend file (the last 20 kept); warns for each regression since the last.
- `regressions` (function): The metrics that grew over `limit` (a fraction) from `before` to `after`, as text.
- `TREND_FILE` (const): The trend file, under the repository.
- `TREND_LIMIT` (const): Growth since the run before that `PERF_TREND` warns about: 15%.
- `Way` (type): A way of measuring (see the file comment).
- `withinBudget` (function): Whether `value` is within `limit`, `tolerance` (a fraction) over it allowed.

### [`tools/cmd/port.ts`](../tools/cmd/port.ts)

- `BLOB_SCRIPTS` (const): The Blob scripts: the stress world's slime hop, kicks to the squash spring, and look turns.
- `blobScript` (function): One Blob script from a fresh `new E.Blob()`, sampled after every step.
- `buildFiles` (function): Every file of `PORT_DIR` but the checksums and `clips/`, by name, generated from the checkout at `sourcePath`.
- `BUILDS` (const): The builds of the humanoid matrix and of the moves.
- `check` (const): The `port` plugin of `x check`: the committed vectors still match their checksums.
- `CHECKSUMS` (const): The file in `PORT_DIR` that records every other file's sha256.
- `checkVectors` (function): Compares the vectors under `root` with their checksums, offline: a changed, missing or unlisted file fails.
- `colorVectors` (function): `color.json`: the colour helpers over a fixed list of colours, 24 of them drawn from `E.rng(0x5eed)`.
- `coreVectors` (function): `core.json`: `rng`, `hash2`, `noise2`, and the math helpers WP 1.1 ports.
- `default` (default): Records the reference vectors the ports from my-3d2dge are tested against (PLAN.md WP 0.11, §9.0): the old engine's own outputs as text JSON in `tests/baselines/port/`, with a generated README that says what each file holds, the source commit, the sampling and the conversion to my-3dge's frame (Appendix C).
- `everyNth` (const): The steps sampled: every 4th at facing 0, every 40th (among those) at the other seven, which differ only by the turn.
- `humanoidRun` (function): One run of the humanoid matrix: a fresh rig of `build` in `state`, facing `facing`·π/4, for 120 steps.
- `humanoidVectors` (function): `humanoid-<build>.json`: every state at every facing.
- `layout` (function): Writes JSON in a stable layout: a container that fits in 120 columns stays on one line, and so does any array of scalars (one sample per line); the others open one item per line, indented by two spaces.
- `LoadedEngine` (type): The old engine in its own `vm` context: `E`, what it printed (must stay empty), and `seed(id)` for each record.
- `loadEngine` (function): Loads `my-3d2dge:engine/my-3d2dge.js` from the checkout at `sourcePath` into a fresh `vm` context.
- `moveRecord` (function): `E.move(name, u, phase)` for u = i/20 on `build`, each sample on a fresh rig at rest at t = 0 (see the README).
- `moveVectors` (function): `moves.json`: every move of `E.MOVES`, its spec as `E.move` builds it, in every phase on every build.
- `PORT_DIR` (const): Where the vectors live, relative to the repository root.
- `SourceEngine` (type): The parts of the old engine's `E` (`My3D2dge`) the vectors call.
- `STATES` (const): The humanoid state matrix (WP 0.11): locomotion, every pose, and both stances (while walking).
- `writeVectors` (function): Writes `files` (names may hold `/`) and their checksums into `dir`, and removes the files an earlier run wrote that are gone now; of the files this run does not `own`, it keeps the recorded checksums.

### [`tools/cmd/qa.ts`](../tools/cmd/qa.ts)

- `compareWithBaselines` (function): Compares a family's violations with its baselines: failures for new or worse ones, warnings for slack entries.
- `default` (default): Runs content QA for the families named, against their baselines (PLAN.md §8.6).
- `loadFamily` (function): Loads `tools/qa/<family>.ts`'s default export.
- `QaBaseline` (interface): An accepted exception in `tests/baselines/qa-<family>[-<area>].json`.
- `QaContext` (interface): What a family is given: the repository root and the id prefixes to keep (empty: every id).
- `qaFamilies` (function): The families in `tools/qa/`, by file name.
- `QaFamily` (interface): A QA family: the default export of `tools/qa/<family>.ts`.
- `QaViolation` (interface): One violation a family found; a larger `value` is worse.
- `readBaselines` (function): Reads every baseline file of `family`, with a failure per malformed file or entry.
- `runQa` (function): Runs one family against its baselines; T1 tests call this (`expect((await runQa(ROOT, 'level')).failures)…`).

### [`tools/cmd/replay.ts`](../tools/cmd/replay.ts)

- `Checked` (interface): What `checkFiles` came to: the outcomes' lines, findings and metrics, and each file's verdict.
- `checkFile` (function): Plays one replay file in every runtime and judges it (see the file comment); writes nothing.
- `checkFiles` (function): Checks every file, then reads `pageErrors` (Chromium's), and only when nothing failed writes the goldens `--update` recorded.
- `default` (default): Replays against their golden hashes (PLAN.md §8.4, §6.5 items 8–9, WPs 1.5 and 2.7).
- `findParting` (function): The first step where any run parts from the first, compared there (`table` reads the components' registry).
- `Outcome` (interface): What one replay came to: its verdict, lines, bisect details, findings, metrics, and goldens to write.
- `parseSwap` (function): Parses `--swap`: `none`, or names from the swap (`sin,pow`).
- `partingLines` (function): The lines that tell a parting: the step, parts, entities and first field, then every field and the inputs.
- `PLATFORM` (const): This platform's golden key: `linux-x64`.
- `replayFiles` (function): The replay files a target names: the file, or every `*.replay.json` under the directory.
- `ReplayOptions` (interface): How replays are checked.
- `Run` (interface): A run of a replay: which runtime, and the hashes it took.
- `RunParting` (interface): Where two runs part: the step, the runs, and what differs there (engine/sim/replay.ts `partingOf`).

### [`tools/cmd/set.ts`](../tools/cmd/set.ts)

- `checkSetting` (function): Types `text` for the setting `path` on a fresh store; throws `UsageError` naming the closest path or the rule.
- `default` (default): Checks a setting against the settings schema, prints it as a URL parameter, and applies it to the page `x inspect` keeps open (PLAN.md §8.1, §3's Agent-operable, I-37, WP 2.7): `node x set box.room.speed 3`.
- `loadSettings` (function): Imports the modules that declare settings, so the shared registry knows them; returns them.
- `sceneModuleOf` (function): The module of `scene`: a module path, a scene id, or the name after an id's colon (`room` for `box:room`).
- `settingModules` (function): The modules that declare settings (`defineSettings(` in their text), tests aside; with `scene`, only its own.
- `settingParam` (function): A setting as a URL parameter: `path=value`, a string as it is, anything else as JSON.

### [`tools/cmd/shot.ts`](../tools/cmd/shot.ts)

- `default` (default): Renders a page on WebGPU in the platform's Chromium and reports what it drew as numbers and text: the look metrics, the ID pass (which object covers which pixels) and a 48 × 27 text thumbnail; images only on demand.
- `encodePng` (function): Encodes RGBA bytes as an 8-bit RGBA PNG (Node's zlib; no image dependency).
- `frameMetrics` (const): The look metrics of a frame of RGBA bytes (engine/gfx/lookMetrics.ts), as the e2e suites import them from here.
- `judgeFrame` (function): The verdict on a frame's look notes: notes that fail are failures, the others warnings.
- `pageUrl` (function): The page's URL path with `scene`, `cam` and each `key=value` of `set` added as URL parameters.
- `READY_TIMEOUT_MS` (const): How long a page may take to signal ready or an error, in milliseconds.
- `resolvePage` (function): Turns a page argument into the URL path to open (relative to the server) and the file that must exist for it.
- `shotMetrics` (function): A shot's numbers for report.json: the look metrics, the ID-pass list and the marks' legend, flat.

### [`tools/cmd/sim.ts`](../tools/cmd/sim.ts)

- `default` (default): Runs a scene headless in Node and prints its hash and events (PLAN.md §8.1, WP 1.5).
- `feelLines` (function): The feel report as two lines of text, rounded for reading (the metrics keep every digit).
- `feelOf` (function): The feel meter's report for a run's first player actor (the inspector member `feel`); a usage error without one.
- `HashedView` (interface): One run's view of a step, with the hash its runtime gave.
- `levelOf` (function): The level a scene loads, for `--map`: registered by its module, else read from its lab's or the fixtures' levels.
- `loadScene` (function): Imports a scene module and picks its scene: `id`, else the one scene it exports.
- `navMap` (function): The text map of `level`'s nav grid under `climb` (the crowd's by default), as `--map` writes it: a key, then one row per map row, and an A* route from the hero's spawn (else the first spawn) to the tile it reaches in the most steps.
- `nodeRuntime` (function): Replays in Node, in this process, on `registry` (the shared one by default): `x replay`'s first runtime.
- `parseSets` (function): `key=value` pairs as path → text; throws `UsageError` for a pair without `=`.
- `replayText` (function): A replay as readable text: its keys in file order, one change-point per line, each platform's hashes one step per line, numbers exact (`-0` kept, engine/core/hash.ts `serialize`).
- `resolveSceneModule` (function): The module a target names: a `.ts` file (its extension optional), a directory's `index.ts`, or a scene id's module.
- `Runtime` (interface): Where replays play: Node in this process, or Chromium in tests/pages/replay.html.
- `sceneModules` (function): Scene id → the module that defines it, from the modules' text (tests aside).
- `sceneRoots` (function): Where scene modules live: `fixtures/scenes/` and every `labs/<name>/scenes/` (tests/pages/replay.ts globs the same).
- `typedSets` (function): `--set` values typed and checked against the settings schema (after the scene module declared its settings).
- `wholeFlag` (function): A whole number from a flag, at least `min`, or `fallback` when the flag is absent.
- `writeReplay` (function): Writes a replay through Prettier with the repository's settings (wherever the file is); true when it changed.

### [`tools/cmd/src.ts`](../tools/cmd/src.ts)

- `default` (default): Prints and checks the read-only source checkouts, `$MY3D2DGE_SRC` and `$SHARDFALL_SRC`, at their pins.

### [`tools/eslint/askTheEntry.ts`](../tools/eslint/askTheEntry.ts)

- `default` (default): The local rule "ask the entry, never the id" (PLAN.md §6.6, ADR-0012): shared code reads an entry's hooks and fields, each with a default on the kind's schema, and never compares a registered id, so new content works without editing the code that uses it.
- `ID_SHAPE` (const): A registered id: a kind, a colon, a name (`move:slash`, `prop:crate`; PLAN.md §6.3).

### [`tools/eslint/banned.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.ts)

- `BANNED_FILES` (const): Where the bans apply.
- `BANNED_IMPORT_FILES` (const): The import bans also cover tests/: a bare `three` in a test page gets its own pre-bundled copy in Vite (WP 0.8).
- `bannedBlocks` (function): The banned-API blocks: imports and names over every file in scope, then syntax and properties by zone.
- `bannedPlugin` (const): The plugin the banned-API blocks use: core's restriction rules as `banned/<rule>`, and `no-namespace-names`.

### [`tools/eslint/family.ts`](../tools/eslint/family.ts)

- `Ban` (type): One entry of a restriction rule's options (`{ selector, message }`, `{ property, message }`…), plus its scope.
- `family` (function): Returns a plugin named `name` whose rules are the named core rules, unchanged.
- `messagesOf` (function): Every `message` in a list of blocks' rule options, `no-restricted-imports`'s paths and patterns included.
- `resolvingImports` (function): `plugin` with its `no-restricted-imports` matching each relative source as resolved from the importing file.
- `shortest` (function): A relative source's shortest spelling from `dir`: `./a/../b` is `./b`, and `../../engine/sim` from `engine/core` is `../sim`.
- `zoned` (function): Blocks that apply one aliased rule over `files` so each file gets exactly the bans that apply to it: one block for all `files`, then one per path an `only` or `except` names, the most specific last (flat config's last block wins).

### [`tools/eslint/index.ts`](../tools/eslint/index.ts)

- `askTheEntryBlocks` (function): The "ask the entry, never the id" block over shared code; `on` is `SWITCHES.askTheEntry` (WP 1.2 turns it on).
- `bannedBlocks` (function from [`tools/eslint/banned.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.ts)): The banned-API blocks: imports and names over every file in scope, then syntax and properties by zone.
- `family` (function from [`tools/eslint/family.ts`](../tools/eslint/family.ts)): Returns a plugin named `name` whose rules are the named core rules, unchanged.
- `layerBlocks` (function from [`tools/eslint/layers.ts`](../tools/eslint/layers.ts)): The layer rules' blocks, in order.
- `local` (const): The local plugin: rules no stock rule expresses, as `local/<rule>`.
- `publicApiBlocks` (function from [`tools/eslint/publicApi.ts`](../tools/eslint/publicApi.ts)): The public-API blocks; `on` is `SWITCHES.publicApi` (on since WP 1.6).
- `simSideBlocks` (function from [`tools/eslint/simSide.ts`](../tools/eslint/simSide.ts)): The sim-side blocks: globals, properties and syntax over all sim-side files, then imports (core/math.ts last).

### [`tools/eslint/layers.ts`](../tools/eslint/layers.ts)

- `layerBlocks` (function): The layer rules' blocks, in order.
- `layerPlugin` (const): The plugin the layer blocks use: core's `no-restricted-imports`, resolving, as `layer/no-restricted-imports`.
- `THREE_MATH` (const): three.js's math classes, the only names `core/math.ts` takes from `three/webgpu` (§6.1); `Color` (from three.js's `src/math/`) since WP 1.1, for engine/core/color.ts (ADR-0020 amendment 1).

### [`tools/eslint/namespaceNames.ts`](../tools/eslint/namespaceNames.ts)

- `EntryName` (interface): One banned name of an entry point: its source, the namespace name the docs use, the name, and the fix.
- `namespaceNames` (const): The rule: options are the banned names (`EntryName`), each reported with its message wherever it is read.

### [`tools/eslint/publicApi.ts`](../tools/eslint/publicApi.ts)

- `publicApiBlocks` (function): The public-API blocks; `on` is `SWITCHES.publicApi` (on since WP 1.6).
- `publicApiPlugin` (const): The plugin the public-API blocks use: core's `no-restricted-imports` (resolving) and `no-unnamed-imports`.
- `SIM_SIDE_GAME_CODE` (const): Sim-side game code: the sim barrel only.
- `unnamedImports` (const): `public-api/no-unnamed-imports`: side-effect imports, dynamic imports with a literal source and TS import types, matched like `no-restricted-imports` matches named ones (options `{ patterns: [{ regex, message }] }`).

### [`tools/eslint/simSide.ts`](../tools/eslint/simSide.ts)

- `SIM_SIDE` (const): Sim-side code: reproducible and renderer-free (PLAN.md §3, "Terms used throughout").
- `simPlugin` (const): The plugin the sim-side blocks use: core's restriction rules as `sim/<rule>`.
- `simSideBlocks` (function): The sim-side blocks: globals, properties and syntax over all sim-side files, then imports (core/math.ts last).

### [`tools/eslint/testing.ts`](../tools/eslint/testing.ts)

- `ALL_ON` (const): Every switch on: the rules written ahead of their code are tested now.
- `Case` (interface): One rule proved both ways.
- `caseProblems` (function): What is wrong with a case's result: its failing source must trip its rule, its passing source lint clean.
- `CaseResult` (interface): A case and the messages ESLint gave its two sources.
- `ConfigModule` (interface): What eslint.config.js exports.
- `describeMessages` (const): One line per message, for readable assertion failures.
- `lintCases` (function): Lints every case's failing and passing source and pairs the results, in the order given.
- `lintFixtures` (function): Lints `files` (repository path → source, each given a file comment) and returns each path's messages.
- `loadConfigModule` (function): Imports the repository's eslint.config.js.
- `Switches` (interface): eslint.config.js's switches.
- `uncovered` (function): The configured messages (from `messages`) that no failing fixture produced.

### [`tools/lib/browser.ts`](../tools/lib/browser.ts)

- `AdapterRecord` (interface): One adapter WebGPU returned: its identity and features.
- `browserRuntime` (function): The browser part of a report's runtime: `141.0.7390.37` → `chromium141`.
- `cachedChromium` (function): Where scripts/setup.sh keeps Chrome for Testing `CHROMIUM_VERSION` on a machine without `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM`.
- `CHROMIUM_VERSION` (const): The platform's Chromium release (tools/deps.json), which scripts/setup.sh fetches where the container's is absent.
- `chromiumPath` (function): The Chromium executable: `$CHROMIUM_PATH`; else `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM` when it exists; else `cachedChromium()` when it exists (a machine outside the container, after scripts/setup.sh); else `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM`, so the launch error names the platform's path.
- `ConsoleRecord` (interface): One console message the page printed.
- `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM` (const): The container's Chromium 141; `$CHROMIUM_PATH` overrides it.
- `describePageError` (function): One line for a page error: its message and where it was thrown (`tests/pages/harness.ts:12:9`).
- `GpuLog` (interface): What WebGPU really did in the page, counted by the probe: `window.__gpu`.
- `initScript` (function): The init script for `page.addInitScript`: the virtual clock seeded with `seed`, then the WebGPU probe.
- `launchBrowser` (function): Launches the platform's Chromium with WebGPU, for `x` commands that open pages.
- `launchOptions` (function): Playwright's launch options for WebGPU on this platform, shared by `playwright.config.ts` and the `x` commands.
- `mapPageError` (function): Maps one uncaught page error to its source frames.
- `mapStack` (function): Maps every frame of a browser stack to its source through the served modules' inline source maps.
- `PageError` (interface): A page error with its stack mapped to sources; `file`, `line` and `column` are its first repository frame.
- `PageWatch` (interface): What `preparePage` collects while the page runs.
- `parseStack` (function): Splits a V8 stack into its frames' function names, URLs and 1-based positions.
- `preparePage` (function): Prepares a page before it loads anything: installs the init script (virtual clock seeded with `seed`, seeded `Math.random` and named streams, the WebGPU probe) and starts collecting console messages and mapped page errors.
- `servedPath` (function): The repository-relative path of a URL the dev server serves (`/@fs/…` included), or the URL itself.
- `SourceFrame` (interface): One frame of a stack, at its source position when a source map gave one.
- `VIEWPORT` (const): The viewport every harness page gets.
- `VirtualClock` (interface): The page's virtual clock and seeded streams, installed as `window.__clock`.
- `WEBGPU_FLAGS` (const): Shardfall's WebGPU flags (PLAN.md §8.8): SwiftShader through Vulkan, presenting to the page's own canvas.

### [`tools/lib/deps.ts`](../tools/lib/deps.ts)

- `compareVersions` (function): Orders two versions: negative when `a` is older.
- `DepsRecord` (interface): `tools/deps.json`.
- `evenLines` (const): Node's releases on even lines only: odd lines never get LTS and are skipped (§6.10, rule 6).
- `firstOfNextLine` (const): The first release of a later line than `version`'s.
- `gitBlob` (const): The git blob id of `bytes`, as `git hash-object` prints it.
- `isDay` (const): Whether `value` is a `YYYY-MM-DD` day.
- `isRelease` (const): Whether `value` is a `{ version, date }` release.
- `Knowledge` (interface): A pinned document that follows a pin's line; `blob` is the git blob of its text after the header comment.
- `lineName` (function): A line's name, for messages and `knowledge`: `3.x`, `0.182.x`, `0.0.4`.
- `lineOf` (function): A version's line, as its lowest version: 3.2.7 → 3.0.0, 0.182.1 → 0.182.0, 0.0.4 → 0.0.4.
- `LockEntry` (interface): One lockfile entry: a package's version and what it depends on (the root entry also lists dev dependencies).
- `Lockfile` (interface): The parts of package-lock.json (v3) the tools read.
- `lookup` (const): Finds a record by name in any section; `node` and `chromium` are the platform's.
- `newestInLine` (const): The newest release of `version`'s line.
- `newestQualified` (const): The newest release that is 12 months old on `day`.
- `NextLine` (interface): The next line's first release, and the day it qualifies.
- `parseVersion` (function): Parses a stable release `x.y.z` (no prerelease), else undefined.
- `PinRecord` (interface): One package's record in `tools/deps.json`.
- `qualifiesOn` (function): The day a release published on `date` turns 12 months old (a 29 February release: 1 March).
- `readRepository` (function): Reads package.json, the lockfile, `tools/deps.json` and `.nvmrc`; throws a message naming the file.
- `RECORD` (const): The record's path, relative to the repository root.
- `RegistryAnswer` (interface): What a registry says about a package: publish times by version, and the published versions and `latest` tag.
- `Release` (interface): A release and the day it was published (`YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC).
- `Repository` (interface): The files `x deps` reads.
- `Rule` (type): How a pin is admitted (PLAN.md §6.10): see tools/cmd/deps.ts's file comment.
- `RULES` (const): Every rule, in the order the plan lists them.
- `satisfies` (function): Whether `version` satisfies an npm range of the forms lockfiles hold: exact, `^`, `~`, `x`, comparators, `||`.
- `SECTIONS` (const): package.json's sections that `tools/deps.json` mirrors.
- `stableReleases` (function): A registry answer's stable, published releases, oldest first, none above its `latest` tag.
- `todayUtc` (const): Today, UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `TYPES` (const): The types packages the rule also covers: `@types/*` and `@webgpu/*`.
- `TypesDep` (interface): A package that a types package pulls in and that is not types itself.
- `typesInLock` (function): The lockfile's types packages (name → versions held), and the packages that are there only because a types package pulls them in (name → version and that types package): reachable from a types package, but not from the root through other packages.

### [`tools/lib/depsCheck.ts`](../tools/lib/depsCheck.ts)

- `checkDeps` (function): The offline dependency check (`x deps --check`; the `deps` plugin of `x check`).
- `CheckDepsOptions` (interface): What the check reads besides the files: the day (UTC) and the active node's version.

### [`tools/lib/depsUpdate.ts`](../tools/lib/depsUpdate.ts)

- `Adoption` (interface): A release to adopt.
- `NETWORK` (const): The real network.
- `NetworkOptions` (interface): What `--update` and `--qualify` take besides the repository.
- `planUpdate` (function): What `--update` would do: the releases to adopt, the refreshed record, and lines to print.
- `Qualified` (interface): One line that has qualified beyond its pin: an upgrade WP to schedule.
- `qualify` (function): `--qualify`: the lines that have qualified beyond each pin (direct dependencies and Node).
- `Registry` (interface): The network, injectable: npm's registry and Node's release index.
- `Runner` (type): Runs a command in the repository and returns its exit status and output.
- `SPAWN` (const): The real runner: a child process in the repository.
- `update` (function): `--update`: adopts what `planUpdate` found (unless `dryRun`), rewrites the record, then runs T0 and T1.

### [`tools/lib/docs.ts`](../tools/lib/docs.ts)

- `directoryOf` (const): The directory of a repository-relative path ('' for the root).
- `DocComment` (interface): A parsed JSDoc comment.
- `DocTag` (interface): One `@tag` of a doc comment, its text as written (indentation kept), and its 1-based line in the file.
- `Example` (interface): One `@example` block.
- `ExportDoc` (interface): One export of a module.
- `isModulePath` (function): Whether a repository-relative path is a module (not a test, fixture, template or declaration file).
- `lineOf` (const): 1-based line of character `index` in `text`.
- `listModules` (function): The repository's modules, sorted.
- `MODULE_ROOTS` (const): The directories whose code files are modules.
- `ModuleDoc` (interface): Everything `x docs` knows about one module.
- `parse` (function): Parses a file with the TypeScript compiler (no type checking).
- `parseDocComment` (function): Parses the raw text of a JSDoc comment that starts on `line`.
- `readModule` (function): Reads one module.
- `readModules` (function): Reads every module of the repository at `root`.
- `ResolvedExport` (interface): One export of a module, followed through re-exports to where it is declared.
- `resolveExports` (function): The exports of a module (a barrel such as engine/index.ts), each followed through re-exports to its declaration.
- `resolveSpecifier` (function): Resolves a relative specifier from `from` to a repository file (extensionless, as Vite and tsx resolve).
- `walk` (function): Every file under `dir` (repository-relative, sorted), skipping `node_modules` and dot-directories.

### [`tools/lib/docsCodes.ts`](../tools/lib/docsCodes.ts)

- `CodeDoc` (interface): One code registered with `defineCodes`.
- `codesOf` (function): The codes registered by the `defineCodes(…)` calls in a parsed module.

### [`tools/lib/docsExamples.ts`](../tools/lib/docsExamples.ts)

- `collectExamples` (function): Every example of the repository's modules (or of `modules`), in module order.
- `compileExample` (function): Transpiles an example (TypeScript allowed) to the JavaScript body `runExample` executes.
- `EXAMPLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (const): The longest an example may run, in milliseconds.
- `ExampleOutcome` (interface): How one example went.
- `rewriteImports` (function): Rewrites the `import` declarations of transpiled JavaScript into `await __import(…)` lines.
- `runExample` (function): Runs one example in this process; never throws.
- `runExamples` (function): The examples' verdicts: Node examples run in order; browser examples are listed for T2.

### [`tools/lib/docsGenerate.ts`](../tools/lib/docsGenerate.ts)

- `apiMarkdown` (function): `docs/API.md`, before formatting.
- `BARRELS` (const): The public barrels (PLAN.md §6.1): game code imports only these.
- `errorsMarkdown` (function): `docs/ERRORS.md`, before formatting.
- `formatMarkdown` (function): Formats Markdown as Prettier would format `file` under `root`.
- `GENERATED` (const): The generated files, by repository path.
- `generateDocs` (function): The generated docs' contents, formatted, by repository path.
- `indexMarkdown` (function): `docs/INDEX.md`, before formatting; `start` is its "Start here" section (tools/lib/docsStart.ts's `startHere`).
- `kindRows` (function): The kinds section of `docs/INDEX.md`: one row per kind declared with `defineKind`, sorted by kind.

### [`tools/lib/docsHelp.ts`](../tools/lib/docsHelp.ts)

- `apiOf` (function): The object's members, sorted: calls as `name()`, properties as `name`, namespaces walked with dotted names.
- `checkHelp` (function): Loads the member modules, starts an empty scene headless and compares `help()` with the object.
- `helpDrift` (function): Where `help()` and the object part, one sentence each ([] when they agree).
- `helpNames` (function): The members a `help()` text lists, sorted: each line's signature, `name()` for a call, `name` for a property.
- `memberModules` (function): The modules under `engine/` and `labs/` (tests aside) that register inspector members, sorted.

### [`tools/lib/docsKinds.ts`](../tools/lib/docsKinds.ts)

- `KindDoc` (interface): One kind declared with `defineKind`.
- `kindsOf` (function): The kinds declared by the `defineKind(…)` calls in a parsed module.

### [`tools/lib/docsPaths.ts`](../tools/lib/docsPaths.ts)

- `checkable` (function): The part of a path to check: the whole path, or the directory above its first placeholder segment.
- `checkPaths` (function): Checks every path, citation and name the comments of `modules` and the covered docs mention.
- `coveredDocs` (function): The documents the path checks read besides the code comments.
- `expand` (function): Expands `{a,b}` and `<a|b>` into every alternative.
- `GENERATED_DIRS` (const): The git-ignored directories tools generate (caches, reports, builds): a fresh checkout lacks them, so they pass.
- `isPlanned` (function): Whether `planned` covers `path` (a file, or a directory ending in `/`): an entry names it or lies inside it, or, for an owned directory (`labs/hello/`, `engine/world/level/**`, `tests/replays/box-1-*.json`), it lies inside one.
- `PathOptions` (interface): Options for `checkPaths`.
- `Planned` (interface): The paths PLAN.md plans: the Owns of WPs not yet done, and §6.2's layout.
- `readPlanned` (function): Reads the planned paths from PLAN.md under `root` (none when it is missing).

### [`tools/lib/docsStart.ts`](../tools/lib/docsStart.ts)

- `Guide` (interface): One task guide: a repository path and what it is for.
- `Skill` (interface): One skill: its name, its SKILL.md path and when to load it.
- `skills` (function): Every skill under `.claude/skills/` in `root`, from its SKILL.md front matter, in name order.
- `SKILLS` (const): The skills' directory.
- `startHere` (function): INDEX's "Start here" section as Markdown lines (links relative to `docs/`), or [] with no guide and no skill.
- `taskGuides` (function): The task guides an AGENTS.md text lists: the `- <path>: <what>` bullets after its "Task guides" line.
- `whenToLoad` (function): A skill's description in short: its first sentence up to a dash (what it is), then the sentence that says when to load it ("Use when…"), when there is one.

### [`tools/lib/escalations.ts`](../tools/lib/escalations.ts)

- `canonicalPrinciple` (function): The canonical spelling of a `principle` value (comma-separated short names, any case); throws naming the closest.
- `deadlineFor` (const): The deadline for a record raised at `raised`: 15 minutes later.
- `DIR` (const): Where the records live, from the repository root.
- `Escalation` (interface): A record's front matter.
- `FIELDS` (const): The front-matter fields, in their written order.
- `generateIndex` (function): The README as `node x esc` writes it: generated from the records under `root`, Prettier-formatted.
- `INDEX` (const): The generated index of the records.
- `indexMarkdown` (function): The README's Markdown before formatting: the records by status, the calls awaiting review first.
- `isoSeconds` (const): A time as the records write it: ISO 8601, UTC, to the second.
- `isOverdue` (const): Whether a record is open past its deadline with no call, at `now`.
- `nextId` (function): The next free id: one past the highest number in use, malformed records included.
- `parseRecord` (function): Splits a record's text into its front matter (unchecked) and body, with the problems found reading it.
- `PRINCIPLES` (const): The doctrine's short names (PLAN.md §3), plus its framing sections, which `principle` may cite.
- `readRecords` (function): Reads every file in `docs/escalations/` but the README, each with the problems found; sorted by name.
- `RecordFile` (interface): A record as read from disk: its file name, its front matter (unchecked) and body, and what is wrong with it.
- `serializeRecord` (function): The record's text: front matter (`FIELDS` in order) then `body`.
- `slugOf` (function): A file-name slug for a question: lower case, words joined by `-`, at most 48 characters, cut at a word.
- `Status` (type): A record's status.
- `STATUSES` (const): A record's statuses, in the order they are reached.
- `validateFields` (function): What is wrong with a record's front matter, read from `file` (its name only); empty when it is well-formed.
- `WAIT_MINUTES` (const): How long the owner has to answer before the agent decides (DOCTRINE.md, Escalation).
- `wellFormed` (function): The records that are well-formed, as front matter, in id order.
- `writeIndex` (function): Rewrites the README when it differs from the records; returns whether it wrote.
- `writeRecord` (function): Writes a record to `docs/escalations/<file>` under `root`.

### [`tools/lib/filmCompare.ts`](../tools/lib/filmCompare.ts)

- `checkFilmThumbs` (function): Records the film's thumbnails as `tests/baselines/thumbs/<name>.json` with `update`, else compares them with it.
- `compareFilmThumbs` (function): Compares each frame's thumbnail with the baseline's (24 of 255): a line per frame that moved, or the counts.
- `compareFrames` (function): Compares frame `a` with the base's frame `b` pixel by pixel, attributing each difference (see the file comment).
- `EMPTY` (const): What a differing pixel that no object's box holds is attributed to.
- `FilmFrame` (interface): One filmed frame: its number, the sim tick, its pixels (row-major RGBA), the ID pass's visible objects, thumbnail.
- `FilmObject` (interface): An object that differs over a film: its pixels, the frames, and whether its ID-pass entry changed (it moved).
- `FilmVerdict` (interface): The verdict on a comparison, its findings, and the objects that differ, most pixels first.
- `FrameDiff` (interface): How a frame differs from the base's: the pixels that differ (-1: not comparable) by object, the changed entries.
- `judgeCompare` (function): Judges a comparison with `ref`: `none` says why there is no baseline, `unchanged` that the sources are the ref's.
- `samePixel` (const): Whether the pixel at byte offset `p` has the same RGBA in both buffers.

### [`tools/lib/filmSheet.ts`](../tools/lib/filmSheet.ts)

- `contactSheet` (function): Lays frames out in `cols` columns, each labelled; with the base's frames and the diffs, rows A, B and the diff.
- `drawText` (function): Draws `text` in upper case on `sheet` at `at`, each font pixel 2 × 2, cut before x `clip`; `?` for other glyphs.
- `LABEL` (const): The height of a label under a frame, in pixels: the 3 × 5 font at twice its size, with a margin.
- `MAGENTA` (const): The colour of a pixel that differs from the base's, on the sheet's diff row.
- `Sheet` (interface): A contact sheet, or any RGBA image: its size and its pixels, row-major.

### [`tools/lib/hash.ts`](../tools/lib/hash.ts)

- `fnv1a` (function): Hashes a string (as UTF-8) or bytes with 32-bit FNV-1a, continuing from `seed` (the FNV offset basis by default).
- `fnv1aHex` (function): `fnv1a` as eight lowercase hex digits, the form reports and logs print.

### [`tools/lib/page.ts`](../tools/lib/page.ts)

- `BrowserMode` (type): How `--browser` plays in Chromium: the sim-only page, or the scene's own page while it renders.
- `labPageOf` (function): The page that draws the scenes of a module under `labs/<name>/scenes/`: `labs/<name>/`; throws for other modules.
- `PageEngine` (type): `window.__engine` as the tools call it in a page.
- `pageRuntime` (function): `x replay --browser page`'s runtime: each replay in its scene's page (`labPageOf`), opened on the replay's own scene (`scenePath`, since a page draws one scene and plays only its replays), drawn after every step.
- `readSignals` (function): Reads `window.__engine`'s signal in `tab`; undefined before the page publishes one.
- `READY_MS` (const): How long a page may take to signal ready or an error, ms.
- `replayBrowser` (function): Chromium with its own Vite server for `x replay --browser`: tests/pages/replay.html (`window.__replay`) under the swap `swap` names, or the scenes' own pages (`pageRuntime`).
- `scenePath` (function): The path of the page that draws a replay's scene: `labs/box/` and `box:spinners` give `labs/box/?scene=spinners`.
- `Signals` (interface): A page's ready-or-error signal (PLAN.md §8.3), read once.
- `waitReady` (function): Waits until `tab` signals ready or an error, or throws an uncaught error, or `ms` pass; returns the last signal.

### [`tools/lib/png.ts`](../tools/lib/png.ts)

- `decodePng` (function): Decodes a non-interlaced 8-bit RGB or RGBA PNG (what Chromium's screenshots are) into RGBA bytes.

### [`tools/lib/report.ts`](../tools/lib/report.ts)

- `Artifact` (interface): A file a command wrote, for example a PNG, with what it shows.
- `Finding` (interface): One failure or warning: what was expected and what happened, where, and the likely fix, as a plain sentence.
- `makeReport` (function): Builds a complete report from the parts a command knows, filling the version, the runtime and empty lists.
- `outputPath` (function): Where the dispatcher keeps every line of a command's output when it cuts what it prints: beside the report.
- `packageVersion` (function): Reads the engine's version from `package.json` under `root`.
- `Report` (interface): The fixed schema of `out/<cmd>/<target>/report.json`.
- `reportPath` (function): The repository-relative path of a command's report: `out/<cmd>/<target>/report.json`.
- `runtime` (function): Names the platform: `linux-x64 node24.21.0`, followed by `browser` (such as `chromium141`) when one was used.
- `targetSlug` (function): Turns a command's target (a page, a scene, a file) into one safe directory name; no target gives `all`.
- `validateReport` (function): Checks a parsed report against the schema; returns one sentence per problem, or an empty list.
- `writeReport` (function): Validates `report`, writes it to `out/<cmd>/<target>/report.json` under `root`, copies it to `out/latest.json` (with its `report` path) and returns the repository-relative path.

### [`tools/lib/source.ts`](../tools/lib/source.ts)

- `repoSlug` (function): `owner/repo` for a GitHub URL: what the session must include when the source cannot be reached.
- `requireSource` (function): Returns the absolute path of the named source (`my-3d2dge` or `shardfall`) for a test that reads it.
- `ResolvedSource` (interface): How a source resolved.
- `ResolveOptions` (interface): Options for `resolveSource`; tests point them at temporary repositories.
- `resolveSource` (function): Resolves one source as `scripts/setup.sh` does, cloning and detaching `.cache/src-*` when needed.
- `SkippableTest` (interface): The part of a Vitest test context that `requireSource` uses (kept structural, so this file never imports Vitest).
- `SourceSpec` (interface): One source checkout, as `scripts/setup.sh` declares it.
- `sourceSpecs` (function): Parses the `resolve_source VAR DEST COMMIT LOCAL_CLONE URL` lines of `scripts/setup.sh` under `root`.

### [`tools/lib/tiers.ts`](../tools/lib/tiers.ts)

- `Base` (interface): The commit a selection compares against, and why it is that one.
- `BudgetCheck` (interface): A tier's duration against its budget.
- `changedFiles` (function): What differs from `base` in `root`'s working tree (see the file comment).
- `Changes` (interface): What changed since a base.
- `checkBudget` (function): Checks one duration against its tier's budget: over it warns, at `FAIL_FACTOR` times it fails.
- `checkReports` (function): Checks each tier's duration: `measured` first (T0 writes no report, so `x ci --local` times it), else the tier's JSON report under `root`.
- `duration` (function): `8.1 s`, `2 min 5 s`, `6 min`.
- `FAIL_FACTOR` (const): A tier at this multiple of its budget, or more, fails; over the budget alone warns.
- `findBase` (function): The base for selections in `root` (see the file comment).
- `isVersionOnly` (function): True when every changed line of a unified diff is a `"version": "…"` line, as many removed as added.
- `LAST_GREEN` (const): Where the last green `x ci --local` records its commit, relative to the root.
- `LONG_RUNS` (const): The long runs (PLAN.md §8.2): no budget, run at each gate.
- `plan` (function): The base, the changes and both selections for `root`: what `x ci --local` and an iterating agent run.
- `recordGreen` (function): Records `sha` as the last green `x ci --local`, the base until main holds a gate.
- `reportMs` (function): The wall-clock duration a Vitest or Playwright JSON report records; throws on anything else.
- `Selection` (interface): What a tier runs for a change, and why.
- `selectT1` (function): What T1 runs for `changes`; undefined changes (no base) run it all.
- `selectT2` (function): What T2 runs for `changes`; undefined changes (no base) run it all.
- `T1_FULL` (const): Changes that run every T1 test: what all of them run under, or read outside their imports.
- `T2_FULL` (const): Changes that run all of T2: code that reaches the browser through the dev server, and what every spec runs under.
- `Tier` (interface): One tier: its full command, its budget and the JSON report its duration is read from.
- `TierId` (type): A tier with a budget.
- `TIERS` (const): The tiers of PLAN.md §8.2.
- `Timing` (interface): One row of the timing table.
- `timingTable` (function): The timing table: one line per step (verdict, name, duration, budget), then the total.
- `Trigger` (interface): A path whose change runs a whole tier: a file, or a directory when it ends in `/`.
- `vitestRerunTriggers` (function): `T1_FULL` as Vitest's `forceRerunTriggers` globs, so `vitest --changed` and `vitest related` agree with `selectT1`.

### [`tools/lib/vite.ts`](../tools/lib/vite.ts)

- `DevServer` (interface): A running dev server.
- `freePort` (function): Asks the system for a free TCP port on 127.0.0.1.
- `startVite` (function): Starts Vite on the repository at `root` (default: this repository), on `port` (default: any free port).

### [`tools/qa/audio.ts`](../tools/qa/audio.ts)

- `AUDIO_LIMITS` (const): The levels and limits the checks use (see the file comment).
- `checkSounds` (function): The violations of every sound on `registry` (or those of `ids`): effects, then songs, each in id order.
- `dbfs` (const): `x` in decibels relative to full scale, one decimal.
- `default` (default): The `audio` QA family (PLAN.md §8.6, WP 9.4, I-23, I-29): `node x qa audio` renders every sound the shared registry has, the engine's `sfx` and `song` entries (engine/audio/data) and a game's (each `*.ts` module under `labs/<name>/sounds/` imported first), and measures each render by numbers: no ear needed (doctrine: Verifiable).
- `fft` (function): In-place radix-2 FFT of `re` and `im`, whose length is a power of two.
- `findClicks` (function): The clicks of `samples`, as sample indices `i`, one per 1 ms: each jump `x[i] − x[i−1]` of at least 0.05 (silence before the start and after the end) into or out of near-silence (the 1 ms before or from it peaking below a sixteenth of the jump) that the waveform does not repeat: no jump of the same sign at least half as large in the 25 ms before an onset, or after a cut.
- `frameSpectrum` (function): The amplitude spectrum of the `size` samples centred on `centre` (zeros beyond the ends), Hann-windowed: `size / 2 + 1` bins `rate / size` apart, about 1 for a full-scale sine on a bin.
- `loadSoundModules` (function): Imports the games' sound modules, so their entries join the shared registry's (whose sound kinds it declares).
- `soundMetrics` (function): Every metric of a render (see `SoundMetrics`).
- `SoundMetrics` (interface): What `soundMetrics` measures.
- `soundModules` (function): A game's sound modules, `labs/<name>/sounds/*.ts` (tests excluded), labs and files in name order.
- `SoundProblem` (interface): A problem a render shows: its metric, its value (larger is worse) and the sentence an agent reads.
- `soundProblems` (function): The problems of a render of a `kind` (`sfx` or `song`) sound, judged by its metrics against `AUDIO_LIMITS`.
- `spectralCentroid` (function): The power-weighted mean frequency of `samples`' spectrum (2048-sample frames, half overlapping), in Hz; 0: silence.

### [`tools/qa/geo.ts`](../tools/qa/geo.ts)

- `checkGeometries` (function): The violations of every geometry on `registry` (or those of `ids`), in id order.
- `checkLevelMeshes` (function): The violations of `level`'s meshes, as item `id`.
- `checkProps` (function): The violations of every prop on `registry` (or those of `ids`), in id order, as the props' ids.
- `default` (default): The `geo` QA family (PLAN.md §8.6, WP 2.4, I-29): `node x qa geo` checks every `geometry` entry the shared registry has (the kit's, engine/gfx/geometry/builtins.ts, and a game's: each `*.ts` module under `labs/<name>/geometry/` imported first), built at its defaults; every `prop` entry's parts (WP 4.5: the engine's, engine/world/props/catalog.ts, and a game's under `labs/<name>/props/`), each built as the prop draws it, under the prop's id; and the level meshes (engine/gfx/level/meshes.ts) of every level file the `level` family reads (tools/qa/level.ts: `labs/box/levels/`, `fixtures/levels/`; a level that does not compile is the `level` family's to report).
- `geometryModules` (function): A game's geometry modules, `labs/<name>/geometry/*.ts` (tests excluded), labs and files in name order.
- `labModules` (function): A game's modules in `labs/<name>/<folder>/*.ts` (tests excluded), labs and files in name order.
- `LEVEL_DRAW_CALLS` (const): Draw calls a level's meshes may cost with one shadow map.
- `LEVEL_VERTICES_PER_TILE` (const): Drawn vertices a level may have per map tile.
- `MAX_SIZE` (const): The longest a geometry may be on any axis (m).
- `PROP_FLOAT` (const): How far (m) a prop's parts may reach below or stop above its base, where its body stands.

### [`tools/qa/level.ts`](../tools/qa/level.ts)

- `default` (default): The `level` QA family (PLAN.md §8.6, WP 2.2, I-29): `node x qa level` validates every level file, the box's (`labs/box/levels/*.txt`, ids `level:<name>`) and the fixtures' (`fixtures/levels/*.txt`, ids `level:fixtures/<name>`; the seeded errors under `fixtures/levels/broken/` are the unit tests' business and are skipped), and runs in T1 through `runQa` (tools/qa/level.test.ts).
- `LEVEL_DIRS` (const): Where level files live, and the id prefix of each place's levels.
- `LevelFile` (interface): One level file: its QA id and its path from the repository root.
- `levelFiles` (function): Every level file under `root`, in `LEVEL_DIRS` order, then by name.

### [`tools/qa/tex.ts`](../tools/qa/tex.ts)

- `checkPropTextures` (function): The violations of the textures of every prop on `registry` (or those of `ids`), in id order, as the props' ids.
- `checkTextures` (function): The violations of every texture on `registry` (or those of `ids`), in id order.
- `default` (default): The `tex` QA family (PLAN.md §8.6, WP 2.3, WP 7.3, I-20): `node x qa tex` bakes every texture generator the shared registry has, the engine's (engine/gfx/textures/v1.ts, v2.ts) and a game's (each `*.ts` module under `labs/<name>/textures/` imported first), at its default size and at twice it, with seeds 1 and 2, and checks every bake; then, under each `prop` entry's id (WP 4.5; a game's props under `labs/<name>/props/` imported first), the textures its parts' materials name, baked as each material bakes them (its parameters and size), and a `reference` violation for a part naming a material no entry defines.
- `textureModules` (function): A game's texture modules, `labs/<name>/textures/*.ts` (tests excluded), labs and files in name order.
- `textureSheet` (function): The contact sheet of `bakes`: per texture its colour, normal and emissive maps (black when nothing glows), each tiled 2 × 2 and scaled by nearest texels to fit a 128 px panel, keeping its shape (row 0 of a map at the bottom, as it is drawn), and a label.

### [`tools/x.ts`](../tools/x.ts)

- `CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS` (const): How long a test waits on a whole command it runs as a child process (`node x <cmd>`, Vitest, `npx`), in ms: the test's timeout and the child's, killed then, so only a hang trips it.
- `closest` (function): The candidate closest to `wanted`, or undefined when nothing is close (more than half the letters differ).
- `Command` (interface): The shape of a `tools/cmd/<name>.ts` module's default export.
- `CommandContext` (interface): What a command receives: its parsed flags and positionals, and the repository root.
- `commandHelp` (function): Reads one command's help text: its file comment.
- `commandNames` (function): Lists the command names found in `tools/cmd/` (every `<name>.ts` that is not a test).
- `CommandOptions` (type): The flags a command accepts, in `parseArgs`'s format.
- `CommandResult` (interface): What a command returns; the dispatcher turns it into printed lines, a report and an exit code.
- `dispatch` (function): Runs `node x <argv…>`: dispatches to the command, prints its verdict and findings (about 20 lines at most), writes its report, and resolves to the exit code (0 pass, 1 fail, 2 usage error).
- `DispatchOptions` (interface): Where `dispatch` finds commands and sends output; tests replace the parts they need.
- `fileComment` (function): Returns the text of a module's `@file` comment, without the comment markers and the `@file` tag.
- `firstSentence` (function): The first sentence of a command's file comment: its one-line description in `x help`.
- `loadCommand` (function): Loads a command module from `tools/cmd/<name>.ts`.
- `MAX_LINES` (const): The most lines a command prints, the report path included (PLAN.md §8.1: "at most about 20").
- `ROOT` (const): The repository root: the directory holding `x.js`.
- `UsageError` (class): Thrown by a command for a bad argument: the dispatcher prints the message and exits 2.

### [`vite.config.ts`](../vite.config.ts)

- `default` (default): Vite's settings (the dev server and the build) and Vitest's (T1), in one file as Vitest expects (PLAN.md §6.10, WPs 0.2 and 0.12).
